conversation.summary: I read the playbook (docs/mary-voice.md), the phase machine (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts), the grounding code, the turn runner and /api/turn. I sampled 4 live /api/turn calls (the budget was 4 and all 4 are used; exact requests and responses are in scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/live-1..4.log). I also ran the repo's own grounding and repeat functions against edge cases (probe-logic.ts / probe-logic.out.json). Her tone, objection handling and pricing answer are good: live call 4 picked the Growth plan for two locations and said final details come with the invite. The weak point is the funnel itself. The only way to sign up needs business, industry and operations, then a pitch you can't skip, then a wrap question. Her email is asked for last. Someone who says "I've only got a minute, put me on the list" and gives an email still gets "To finish, what's the business, roughly?" (live call 3). If they leave, the outcome is "declined" and the end screen says "No spot reserved". Grounding, the part of MARY that is most her own, still lets invented values through: a made-up email domain, "dental" taken from "a small practice", and a guessed "real estate" accepted on "You know, we mostly do cars". Measured time to her first text was 2.4-7.6 s (before speech-to-text and text-to-speech), against an ~800 ms budget. Retell fixes silence, latency and the repeat machinery. The funnel, the grounding, the opener, the promises and the close are prompt and business logic that have to be carried into the Retell agent on purpose; ready-to-paste text is in scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/proposed-prompt-edits.txt.

findings.title: No fast lane: a visitor who gives name + email and wants to leave cannot get a spot and is recorded as 'declined'
findings.evidence: Live call 3 (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/live-3.log): Person: "I'm Dana. Look, I've only got a minute, can you just put me on the list? It's dana k at gmail dot com." -> MARY: "Yes, Dana — I'll keep this quick; I've got danak at gmail dot com." / "To finish, what's the business, roughly?" (mode=rushed). Required fields include business/industry/operations: src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:90, gate text :131-133 ('even if they ask you to finish now'), complete gated :235, src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:55. Leaving -> declined: mary-prompt.server.ts:119, :224-227. Probe: endingFor({declined:true, collected:{name,email}}) = "declined" (probe-logic.out.json). End screen for declined: text.ts:76-81 'No spot reserved'. Minimum after 'I've only got a minute': reveal reply + lanes reply + wrap reply = at least 3 more turns once business/industry/operations are in, plus 1-2 turns to get those.
findings.user_impact: The visitors most likely to leave (rushed people at the stand) hand over their email and still walk away told 'No spot reserved'. Their row lands as declined. Saying 'To finish' when 3-5 turns are left also breaks trust.
findings.recommendation: Make name + email the minimum sign-up. In mary-prompt.server.ts:90/217-218 and text.ts:55, set the required fields for `complete` to name+email, and flag the lead row as a partial profile when business/industry/operations are missing. Replace the gate text at :131-133 with: 'A spot is secured once you have their name and email… If they want to go and you have name and email: confirm the spot in one line and close. If you have no email yet: ask for it once, tied to the spot, then let them go.' In endingFor, 'leaving' with name+email present returns signed_up, not declined. Exact text in proposed-prompt-edits.txt section 2.

findings.title: Email is asked for last, after discovery, reveal and the lanes pitch, so anyone who drops mid-call leaves no contact
findings.evidence: Phase order: CONTACT is reached only after discoveryDone && revealed && lanesDone (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:118-125). The spec's own worked example asks for email on MARY's 7th turn, after 5 person answers (docs/mary-voice.md:439-459). The reveal/lanes flags only count when 'Convert'/'Cultivate'/'Recover' were heard in full (src/features/mary/conversation/turn-runner.ts:167-170), so a cut-in pushes the email ask back further.
findings.user_impact: A partial row (lead-lifecycle.ts:219-235) from someone who leaves at turn 4 has a name and a business but no way to reach them. That is a lost lead even when the conversation went well.
findings.recommendation: Move the email ask to the peak. The REVEAL turn's followUp becomes 'That's the whole sign-up, by the way. Where should your invite go?' (mary-prompt.server.ts:121 and mary-voice.md section 5, dropping the rule 'Never followed immediately by an ask'). LANES comes after and is skipped when mode is rushed. In rushed or leaving mode, ask for the email right after the name. Proposed text in proposed-prompt-edits.txt section 3.

findings.title: Visitors with no business (student, job-seeker, curious) can never join, contradicting the playbook
findings.evidence: docs/mary-voice.md:221-222: 'If they have no business at all… don't invent one, and still offer them the spot.' The prompt says the opposite: src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:119 'If they have no business at all… switch to EXIT… set declined true', and business/industry/operations are required for complete (:90, :235; text.ts:55).
findings.user_impact: Every event has curious visitors and job-seekers. The model gets two opposite instructions, so what happens depends on the model, and the code path always ends as declined. That is a lost sign-up and a confusing goodbye.
findings.recommendation: Follow the playbook: with name+email they get the spot (same change as the fast-lane finding). Change mary-prompt.server.ts:119 to 'If they have no business at all, say that's fine, skip discovery and the reveal, and hold their spot with their email.'

findings.title: Turn latency is 2.4-7.6 s to the first text, with no filler, and the fixed-content opener is generated by the LLM
findings.evidence: Live /api/turn timings (live-1..4.log), time to first 'say' / full turn: opener 4,638/5,806 ms; 'what is this' 2,655/4,325 ms; early leaver 2,356/3,662 ms; dump+price 7,617/9,728 ms. Excludes /api/transcribe before and TTS after. Causes: forceReasoning (src/routes/api/turn.ts:48-49), a 24-field schema whose followUp can only be spoken once the whole object is done (mary-prompt.server.ts:22-67; turn-runner.ts:155-157), an LLM-generated welcome (turn-runner.ts:52-54, mary-app.tsx:533), and only a 'thinking' orb in the meantime (turn-runner.ts:100). Budget: 'roughly 800 milliseconds before a conversation starts to feel slow' (https://webrtc.ventures/2026/09/voice-ai-latency-budget/, 2026-09-23). Once sheets are configured, experienceForTurn can add up to 900 ms on a cache miss (src/lib/mary-experience.server.ts:258-288).
findings.user_impact: 4-8 s of silence after every answer, plus transcription and speech time. In a loud room people repeat themselves or walk off. The 4.6 s wait after tapping Start is the first impression.
findings.recommendation: Make the opener a fixed line, spoken the moment Start is tapped (pre-generate or cache its audio). For the typing path, which keeps /api/turn: drop forceReasoning or use a faster model for turns, and move the evidence fields behind say/followUp so followUp is final before the bookkeeping is written. In Retell, use a static begin_message (a dynamic opener also triggers the 10 s minimum charge, https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/billing-exceptions). Measure time to first audio, not Retell's claim: vendor figure ~600 ms, independent median TTFAB 1,740 ms (https://openbenchmarks.com/voice-agent-latency/retell).

findings.title: Grounding records business/industry values that the quoted words don't support ('dental' from 'a small practice')
findings.evidence: src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:328-336 only checks that the evidence quote occurs in the person's words, never that the value follows from it. Probe (probe-logic.out.json): userMessages ['I run a small practice.'], proposed industry 'dental', business 'Smile Dental Group', operations 'front desk calls every lead back by hand', all with evidence 'I run a small practice' -> all three accepted, rejected []. The vertical guard covers only real estate/finance words (mary-grounding.ts:129-154), while the playbook forbids guessing dental, auto, HVAC and staffing too (docs/mary-voice.md:217-218). No unit test covers this (tests/unit/grounding.test.ts).
findings.user_impact: The sheet and the reveal ('I've got your business…') can hold a business name and trade the person never said. That breaks the product's main promise that she only records what was said, in front of the prospect.
findings.recommendation: In the default case, also require the value to be supported: for business, at least 50% of the value's content tokens appear in the person's words; for industry, the head word or a mapped synonym appears in the person's words. Extend VERTICAL_VALUE to every vertical the playbook names. Add unit tests for these probe cases. For Retell Option B, add <field>_evidence params to save_lead and run groundCollected on the user lines of call.transcript, which every custom-function request includes (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/custom-function).

findings.title: Email grounding accepts an invented domain, and voice capture has no spell-and-confirm step
findings.evidence: src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:298-304: ok if the squashed user text contains just the local part (length >= 2). Probe: user said 'Sarah.' / 'Just use my work email.', model proposed 'sarah@gmail.com' -> accepted. Live call 3 turned 'dana k at gmail dot com' into 'danak@gmail.com' and moved straight on without asking whether it was right. Retell recommends reading back critical details and spelling them (Agent Handbook 'Echo Verification' / 'NATO Phonetic Alphabet', https://docs.retellai.com/build/agent-handbook).
findings.user_impact: A wrong or made-up address makes the lead unreachable even though the visitor did everything right, and nobody notices until launch mail bounces.
findings.recommendation: Drop the local-part-only branch (require the full address, or at least the domain too). Add to the email beat: 'Read it back in chunks and spell anything that isn't an ordinary word, then ask "Did I get that right?" (the one allowed confirmation question). If it's wrong twice, ask them to type it in the box.' Show an email input on screen during the email ask so speech-to-text is skipped entirely. In Retell, also enable Echo Verification.

findings.title: Sideways replies count as 'yes' and confirm her guess, bypassing the real-estate guard
findings.evidence: AFFIRMATION_START includes 'you', 'basically', 'pretty', 'more', 'right', 'sure' (src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:15-44); isAffirmation only rejects on a negation word. Probe: 'You know, we mostly do cars', 'Basically we're a law firm', 'Pretty much the opposite, we do cars' and 'Right, we're a law firm' are all read as yes. With MARY's last line 'Let me guess — real estate…?', the reply 'You know, we mostly do cars' records industry 'real estate', because the affirmation exception at :210 overrides assumesVertical.
findings.user_impact: She confidently records the vertical the person just corrected, and then sells to it. This is the exact default-to-real-estate failure the guard was written to stop.
findings.recommendation: Treat those words as a yes only when the reply is 3 tokens or fewer, or has no other content nouns; otherwise treat it as an answer. Add the probe sentences to tests/unit/grounding.test.ts. In Retell, the same logic runs in the save_lead handler.

findings.title: She promises things nothing delivers: a 'confirmation' email and 'the request is with the team'
findings.evidence: Email ask: 'So I know where to send your early-access confirmation' (docs/mary-voice.md:193, :459, :509; mary-prompt.server.ts:125). Nothing sends email: no MailApp/GmailApp/sendEmail in docs/google-sheets/Code.gs or src. Callback final turn says 'the request is with the team' (mary-prompt.server.ts:112), and the close says 'we'll be in touch', both spoken before any save (turn-runner.ts:180-184 -> lead-lifecycle.ts:238-276). Live GET https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/api/lead returned {"configured":false} on 2026-09-26, so nothing reaches the team. The playbook's own rule 'Only say it's recorded after it actually saved' (mary-voice.md:338) is not enforced.
findings.user_impact: Visitors wait for a confirmation that never comes, and callback requesters are told a person has their number when it sits only in their own browser. The broken promise lands on the brand.
findings.recommendation: Change the ask to 'so your invite has somewhere to go' until a confirmation email exists (or add one in Apps Script on append). Speak the 'saved / with the team' line only after the sync answers saved. In Retell, the agent says it only after save_lead returns ok, and uses the position it returns.

findings.title: The opener is jargon, never says what the visitor gets or how long it takes, and doesn't match the landing preview
findings.evidence: Live call 1: "Hi there. I'm MARY, Omnikom's AI Revenue Concierge. OmniSuite is our AI and human revenue engine." / "And what should I call you?" The landing page previews a different opener, "Hi, I'm MARY. Want first access to OmniSuite through the launch waitlist?" (src/features/mary/ui/landing.tsx:9), and promises 'two minutes' (landing.tsx:139-140). The WELCOME instruction has no waitlist, benefit or time (mary-prompt.server.ts:116; mary-voice.md:276-297), yet DISCOVER says 'never mention the waitlist offer again' (:119). Live call 2 shows the natural next question: 'what is this exactly? What am I signing up for?'
findings.user_impact: The first 10 seconds spend the visitor's attention on category words and a name request before saying what they get. Visitors who expected the preview's line have to ask what this is, which costs a turn and some trust.
findings.recommendation: Use a fixed opener: say 'Hi, I'm MARY. I look after early access for OmniSuite, Omnikom's new revenue engine.' / followUp 'Two minutes with me and you're on the list. What should I call you?' Keep 3-4 variants and delete 'never mention the waitlist offer again'. In Retell this becomes begin_message (static, start_speaker agent).

findings.title: The playbook's silence handling is unreachable, so a turn that ends on a statement can stall forever
findings.evidence: The playbook's 'Silence — "Still with me? No rush."' (docs/mary-voice.md:403) never reaches the model: /api/turn runs only on user input (turn-runner.ts:57-72). The client nudges only when the mic is muted or unavailable (src/features/mary/mary-app.tsx:378-396: `if (stage !== "call" || (micLive && !micMuted)) return`). The reveal turn ends on a statement (live call 4 followUp: '…without a form—that's Convert.').
findings.user_impact: With a live mic in hold-to-talk, after a statement like the reveal, nothing tells the visitor it's their turn. Dead air until they guess or leave.
findings.recommendation: In Retell set reminder_trigger_ms ~8000, reminder_max_count 2 (defaults are 10 s and 1) and end_call_after_silence_ms ~45000 (default is 10 min) (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). Add reminder lines: first, restate the last question more simply; second, 'I'll hold your spot if you give me an email, or type it below'. If name+email are already captured, close as signed_up on silence. Until the swap, let the idle timer also fire with a live mic after 20 s of no hold.

findings.title: The prompt contradicts itself: reveal, drive rule, followUp null, word cap, and examples that can't happen at runtime
findings.evidence: REVEAL 'Do not ask for anything in this turn' (mary-prompt.server.ts:121) vs the drive rule 'every turn must END on one concrete move' (:160) vs 'followUp… is null only on a closing, exit or final callback turn' (:164) vs 'Or null when a reaction alone is right' (mary-voice.md:422-424). Word cap 'roughly 25 words for the whole turn' (mary-voice.md:426) vs live replies of 31 (call 2) and 33 words (call 4). Worked examples show MARY taking two turns in a row (mary-voice.md:455-459, 543-546), which the runner can't do. Phase is computed from the fields known before this turn (mary-prompt.server.ts:100-102), so the turn that completes discovery is told 'draw out what is still missing'; in live call 4 the model revealed anyway, against its instruction.
findings.user_impact: Each turn the model has to guess which rule wins, so behaviour differs from call to call: a reveal with or without a question, long turns in a loud room, discovery questions after everything is known.
findings.recommendation: Add REVEAL as an explicit exception to the drive rule. Make the cap hard (≤25 words, LANES ≤35) and check it in finishTurn. Rewrite the examples so every MARY turn follows a Person line. Add: 'If their last message supplies the last missing detail, act on the next phase now.' In Retell, split the phases into multi-prompt states with explicit transitions (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/write-multi-prompt).

findings.title: The repeat detector flags normal short replies, costs an extra LLM call, and feeds a fake 'Person' complaint to the model
findings.evidence: isNearRepeat (src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:33-48) divides by the shorter line. Probe: 'Good to meet you, Sarah.' after 'Hey — good to meet you. I'm MARY…' = repeat (this is the playbook's own example, mary-voice.md:439-443). So are 'Got it.', 'Fair.', "You're all set." and "I'll be quick." when an earlier line contains them. A flagged say is suppressed (turn-runner.ts:124) and triggers a second, non-streamed LLM call (:129-145; full turns measured at 3.7-9.7 s). The retry injects REPEAT_NUDGE as a user line, '(You just repeated yourself…)' (:35-36), which the prompt renders as 'Person:'. The followUp question itself is never checked for repeats.
findings.user_impact: Several extra seconds of silence on ordinary turns. She may apologise to the visitor for a complaint they never made. A real repeated question still gets through.
findings.recommendation: Only flag lines of 6+ words, and check followUp against earlier followUps. Pass the nudge as a system note in buildPrompt, not as a Person line. In Retell Option B this runner is gone; in Option A carry the fixed version.

findings.title: A rushed visitor still gets the full pitch, and a cut-in during the lanes pitch replays it
findings.evidence: Rushed mode only adds 'one short beat, get to the point' (mary-prompt.server.ts:143-147). LANES can't be skipped: CONTACT/WRAP need lanesDone (:122-125). lanesDone needs both words heard in full (turn-runner.ts:168-170), so an interruption during the pitch replays LANES next turn. The playbook asks for 'In a rush — compress everything… email only, close' (mary-voice.md:410-411) and 'I'm busy — two short turns to the end' (:384-385). The in-a-rush example (mary-voice.md:537-553) shows reveal and lanes as back-to-back MARY turns, which the runner can't do.
findings.user_impact: The people with the least patience hear the longest sales beat, sometimes twice. That is the moment they cut in or walk off.
findings.recommendation: Skip LANES when mode is rushed, or when a lanes line was already cut off once. Count it as done if either loop word was heard. The rushed path is name -> email -> one-line reveal -> close.

findings.title: The close doesn't confirm details back and gives no concrete next step or position
findings.evidence: WRAP only asks 'if they have questions or want you to finalise their spot' (mary-prompt.server.ts:128), with no recap. CLOSE is fixed: 'Thanks for signing up — we'll be in touch as soon as OmniSuite launches, a product by Omnikom.' (:127; mary-voice.md:312-314). The end screen already shows a position and 'Invitations go out in order of position' (text.ts:83-93; end-screen.tsx:91), but she never says them. Retell's prompt guide: 'Confirm understanding: Paraphrase important information back to the caller' (https://docs.retellai.com/build/prompt-engineering-guide).
findings.user_impact: The visitor leaves unsure what was recorded or what happens next. The last spoken words are a brand tagline instead of their spot.
findings.recommendation: WRAP becomes a one-line recap: name, business and the email read back, then 'Anything you want to ask before I lock it in?' CLOSE, after the save returns: 'You're in, {name} — number {position} on the list. Your invite comes to that email when early access opens.' Keep 'a product by Omnikom' on screen only. In Retell, save_lead returns the position (retell-migration.md step 5) and end_call fires after this line.

findings.title: Porting the playbook as-is to Retell would raise per-minute cost and keep lines that assume the hold-to-talk button
findings.evidence: The system prompt is the whole playbook: 28,135 chars, ~7,000 tokens (docs/mary-voice.md via mary-prompt.server.ts:4,9), plus ~1k tokens of per-turn rules. Retell bills duration × (prompt tokens ÷ 4,000) above 4,000 tokens, and the count includes the transcript (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/billing-exceptions), so every call starts at ≥1.75× billed duration and grows. Hold-button lines: mary-voice.md:3-4 and :343-344 ('ask them to hold the button'). The migration plan pulls post-call analysis fields industry/business (docs/architecture/retell-migration.md:97-99), which are ungrounded LLM extractions.
findings.user_impact: Higher running cost, MARY telling people to press a button that no longer exists, and invented industries coming back into the sheet from call analysis.
findings.recommendation: Port as a multi-prompt agent with a global prompt under 4,000 tokens. Move objection lines to per-state prompts and drop worked examples from the always-on context. Rewrite the hold-button lines. Name tools explicitly in the prompt, per Retell's guide: 'call save_lead as soon as name and email are confirmed…; call end_call after the close/exit/final callback line'. Use call_analyzed only for summary/outcome and never overwrite grounded fields. Before launch, run Retell LLM simulation cases for every scenario in these findings (https://docs.retellai.com/test/llm-simulation-testing).

findings.title: Her phone number is never offered when the email arrives before the email-ask step
findings.evidence: allCaptured leaves phone out (mary-prompt.server.ts:89-91). The email-ask phase (:124-125), the only place the phone is offered, is skipped once the email is in. Live call 3 captured the email in the first answer, so this visitor would go discovery -> reveal -> lanes -> WRAP without a phone offer. The playbook says phone is 'always offered' (mary-voice.md:144, :513-516).
findings.user_impact: Fewer callable leads for the sales team. Small, since phone is optional.
findings.recommendation: Offer the phone once as the followUp of the turn that confirms the email ('Number's optional — want to add one?'), whatever the phase.

funnel.summary: I walked the live site (https://omnisuite.omnikom.io, the PR #1 build; its UI files are identical to PR #2) as an iPhone 13, an iPhone SE-sized screen and desktop Chrome, from the landing page through Start, the mic prompt (allowed, denied, and answered slowly), the first 30 seconds, turn-taking, a full sign-up, a decline and "Type instead". Every /api route was mocked except two live calls I made to measure real latency (1 /api/turn welcome and 1 /api/speech; the budget was 4). I never sent a POST to /api/lead and never sent a beacon. Screenshots, logs and scripts (funnel.mjs, tap-test.mjs, double-tap.mjs, slow-net.mjs) are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/ ("shots/..." below means that folder). Verdict: the landing page looks polished and makes the ask clear, but the funnel breaks at both ends. At the end, every visitor is told "Early access confirmed" with a position number that the code makes up, while the live lead store is not connected (GET /api/lead returns {"configured":false}) and no confirmation email exists anywhere. Along the way: MARY's first word comes about 4.6 s after the tap and her first question about 16-18 s after it; a natural tap on the big button during her greeting cuts her off and leaves the call silent; a denied mic leads to a dead end; tapping Start twice runs two welcomes; and there is no notice anywhere that the call is AI-processed or recorded, or how the data is used. Retell fixes the latency and the hold-button traps. It does not fix the lead, consent, denial, double-start or end-screen problems, and Retell's own terms of service and its record-everything default make the consent gap more urgent.

findings.title: End screen confirms a spot and shows a made-up position number while the live site stores no lead
findings.evidence: Live GET https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/api/lead -> {"configured":false} (2026-09-26). src/features/mary/conversation/lead-lifecycle.ts:125 (not configured -> sync 'local', position: entry.position) and :129 (falls back to the local number even when the sheet saves without a position); src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:122-126 (positionFor = 128 + hash % 640) and :134 (the position is set on the first save, before any email is known, so it is seeded from the session id). The same email sarah@brightpath.com got 'Early access position #327' on iPhone and '#156' on desktop: shots/convo-ios-22-end-full.png, shots/convo-desktop-21-end-settled.png. The copy 'EARLY ACCESS CONFIRMED / You're on the list / Invitations go out in order of position' comes from src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:84-92. The row exists only in the visitor's own localStorage (log-convo-ios.json: keys ['omnisuite.waitlist.v1']).
findings.user_impact: Every visitor who finishes the call today is told they are confirmed with a queue number, but the owner never receives the lead, and the number changes every session. The funnel's single outcome is lost, and anyone who compares numbers or never hears back will stop trusting the product.
findings.recommendation: Short term: when result.sync is 'local' or 'failed', do not show 'confirmed' or a position. Show 'We couldn't save your spot, tap to retry / leave your email' and retry syncLead. Remove the positionFor fallback in lead-lifecycle.ts:125/129 and only show a position the server returned. Longer term: connect SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL (decision D2) and test one real lead end to end. With Retell, keep the rule that MARY never says a position unless save_lead returned one from the sheet.

findings.title: A tap (not a hold) on the big green button during MARY's welcome cuts her off and leaves the call silent
findings.evidence: tap-test.mjs on the live site (iPhone profile): a 120 ms tap 5 words into the welcome cut her to 'Hello. I'm MARY, Omnikom's …'. No follow-up question was spoken and nothing happened for the next 8 s (/api/speech count stayed at 1). Screenshot shots/tap-ios-after-tap-during-welcome.png. Code: press -> runner.interrupt() (src/features/mary/mary-app.tsx:184-191), and the follow-up is dropped (turn-runner.ts 'if (turn.followUp && !deps.isHeld())'). A hold shorter than MIN_HOLD_MS (300 ms) just calls onCancel -> waiting(), with no notice (src/features/mary/voice/hold-talk.ts:4,123-124; mary-app.tsx:175-179,196).
findings.user_impact: Tapping is the natural gesture on the screen's biggest control, which reads 'Hold to talk to MARY' while she speaks for about 10 s. Anyone who taps loses her name question and sees a half-finished sentence with no next step during the first 15 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Treat a hold shorter than 300 ms as 'no-op plus hint': do not interrupt her. Only call runner.interrupt() once the hold passes MIN_HOLD_MS, and flash 'Press and hold while you speak'. If she was cut off with no user text, resume or repeat her last question. Also show the button as 'MARY is talking…' (dimmed) until her turn ends.

findings.title: About 4.6 s of silence before MARY's first word and about 16-18 s before she asks anything
findings.evidence: Live measurements (2 of the 4 allowed calls): /api/turn welcome first 'say' at 2.98 s, full turn at 4.15 s (turn-welcome.ndjson); /api/speech first audio at 1.28 s, 24-word line = 10.2 s of audio (speech-welcome.timing). Replayed with those delays in the browser: tap -> first word revealed +4.6 s on iPhone and desktop (log-voice-ios.json, log-voice-desktop.json). Welcome ends +14 s, then a 1.8 s silent gap while the follow-up is synthesised: the follow-up TTS is only requested after the first line ends (turn-runner.ts deliver followUp after wait(260); audio-engine.ts speak() fetches per line, no prefetch). The question 'And what should I call you?' is audible at +15.8 s (iPhone) and the 'your turn' cue appears at +18.4 s (desktop). The greeting is generated by the LLM on every call (turn-runner.ts welcome() -> /api/turn with forceReasoning in src/routes/api/turn.ts). Real iPhones add the permission sheet on top.
findings.user_impact: Visitors wait in silence ('…' on screen) for almost 5 s, then listen to a 10 s company description before being asked anything. This is the point where people bail or start tapping.
findings.recommendation: Now: play a pre-rendered greeting clip (static TTS of a short opener, cached) the moment the call screen opens, and fetch the first LLM turn in parallel. Shorten the welcome to about 5 s ('Hi, I'm MARY, OmniSuite's AI concierge. What should I call you?'). Request the follow-up TTS while the first line is still playing. With Retell: use a static 'Custom message' begin message and set begin_message_delay_ms to about 1000-1500. Retell staff (community thread, 2026-09-17) confirmed the first packet reaches the browser about 1250 ms after the agent starts talking, so without the delay the first word is clipped. Port the short opener into the Retell prompt.

findings.title: Mic denied: wrong generic message, a 'mic button' that doesn't exist, and a Hold button that silently does nothing
findings.evidence: Runs deny-ios / deny-desktop (getUserMedia rejects NotAllowedError). The visible notice was 'I couldn't open the microphone. Tap the mic button to try again, or keep going by typing.' (log-deny-ios.json). The specific 'denied' copy from start() (mary-app.tsx:521) is overwritten by the hold recorder's raw DOMException (src/features/mary/voice/hold-recorder.ts:118 calls getUserMedia unwrapped -> mary-app.tsx:254 micMessage(error) -> reason 'unknown', text.ts:115). In the default hold mode there is no mic button (composer.tsx:230 renders it only when !holdMode). The Hold button stays the primary CTA and pressing it produces no visible change: shots/deny-desktop-11-deny-holding.png, shots/deny-ios-10-your-turn.png. The status line still says 'Hold the button while you talk'; MARY carries on as if she can hear them, and the idle nudge says 'you can talk to me' (text.ts:138).
findings.user_impact: Visitors who block the mic (or are in an in-app browser) get contradictory instructions and a button that does nothing. The typing fallback exists but is presented as secondary, so many will leave.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the recorder's getUserMedia with micFailureFrom / MicUnavailableError. On 'denied', switch the call to typing mode: hide the Hold button, focus the textarea, and show a card with per-browser steps (Safari: aA > Website Settings > Microphone > Allow; Chrome: lock icon > Microphone). Keep the permissions-change listener that already re-enables voice (mary-app.tsx:325-348). Have MARY say one line: 'Looks like I can't hear you, no problem, type below.' With Retell, mic denial fires onError and then onEnd, ending the session (docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call), so catch it and continue the same conversation in the /api/turn text chat.

findings.title: No notice that the call is recorded, transcribed or processed by third parties, and no privacy link
findings.evidence: grep over src/features, src/components and src/routes for privacy|terms|recorded|recording|consent: no user-facing hits. Landing text (log-landing-ios.json) is only 'Your AI Revenue Concierge. Talk to her for two minutes…'; the page has 0 links. The data actually captured: the full transcript, name, email, phone, userAgent, referrer and timezone go to the sheet (lead-sync.ts browserContext, lead-lifecycle.ts:52-78). Transcripts go to /api/reflect to create 'lessons' (mary-app.tsx:95-119). Partial transcripts are beaconed as 'abandoned' when the tab closes (lead-lifecycle.ts flush). Audio goes to the Lovable AI gateway (routes/api/transcribe.ts). Retell: data_storage_setting defaults to 'everything' (recordings + transcripts; docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-web-call, docs.retellai.com/accounts/privacy-disable). Retell ToS (updated 2026-06-01): 'If Customer enables call recording, Customer must disclose the recording … and obtain any consent required … before or at the start of the call', and calls may be used for model training unless opted out (retellai.com/legal/terms-of-service). EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency duties have applied since 2 Aug 2026 (labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org research note 2026-07-29; digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu FAQ). ElevenLabs requires its agents to show the recording notice 'immediately prior to any interaction' (elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/legal/disclosure-requirement).
findings.user_impact: Business visitors, the target audience, are asked for email and phone by a voice bot with no word on recording or data use. That hurts trust at the moment of commitment, and after the Retell switch it breaks the vendor's terms.
findings.recommendation: Add one line under the Start buttons, before any audio: 'MARY is an AI. Your conversation is transcribed and saved so our team can follow up; see Privacy.' Link to a short privacy page covering what is stored, where (sheet, AI providers), for how long, and how to delete it. Add the same notice to MARY's opener or to Retell's begin message (Retell's own recommendation). For Retell, choose data_storage_setting and data_storage_retention_days deliberately and opt out of training if you don't want it.

findings.title: Tapping Start twice while the mic prompt is open starts two welcomes, and MARY asks the name twice
findings.evidence: double-tap.mjs (desktop, mic prompt answered after 4 s, second click at +1.6 s): getUserMedia called 2x, /api/turn 2x, plus one /_serverFn maryTurn retry (a paid LLM call on the live site; mocked here), and the transcript shows 'Hello. I am MARY. / What should I call you? / What should I call you?' (shots/doubletap-desktop-result.png). During the wait the landing shows no pending state (shots/doubletap-desktop-waiting-for-permission.png). Cause: start() only checks stage === 'landing', and the stage stays 'landing' until after `await unlockAudio(); await primed` (src/features/mary/mary-app.tsx:508-534). The button has no disabled or loading state (src/features/mary/ui/landing.tsx:146-157). The first primed stream is overwritten, so the first mic is leaked.
findings.user_impact: Chrome's mic bubble is small and easy to miss, so a second click is likely. The visitor then gets a doubled, confusing greeting, possibly a stuck mic indicator, and the operator pays twice.
findings.recommendation: Set a 'starting' flag synchronously on the first tap (in the store or a ref), disable both CTAs and show 'Allow the microphone to talk to MARY…' next to the button while permission is pending. Make primeMicPermission share one in-flight promise. With Retell, the same guard must stop a second POST /api/retell/web-call, which would open two billed calls with two MARYs talking.

findings.title: No confirmation email and no way to fix misheard details: the visitor leaves with nothing
findings.evidence: MARY asks for the email 'so I know where to send your early-access confirmation' (docs/mary-voice.md worked example; src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:125), and the end screen says 'Your position comes with the confirmation' (src/features/mary/ui/end-screen.tsx:100). Yet no email is sent anywhere: grep for MailApp/GmailApp/sendEmail finds nothing in src/ or docs/google-sheets/Code.gs. 'Details confirmed' is a static list (end-screen.tsx:156-173) with no edit option. The only action is 'Start another conversation', which calls newSession() and reloads, wiping everything (mary-app.tsx:591-595; end-buttons in log-convo-desktop.json). There is no share or referral link. The desktop layout also breaks the email mid-word ('sarah@brightpath.co / m', shots/convo-desktop-21-end-settled.png).
findings.user_impact: Emails captured by voice are prone to transcription errors, and the visitor sees a wrong address but cannot fix it. Nothing reaches their inbox to prove the signup, and the peak-intent moment has no share step. LaunchList (2026) notes that referral and share prompts work best right at signup.
findings.recommendation: Send a confirmation email when the sheet writes the row (Apps Script MailApp in Code.gs upsertLead, or a transactional email provider) containing the real position and a share link. Add an 'Edit' affordance on each confirmed field that re-syncs through /api/lead. Add 'Share OmniSuite' (Web Share API) on the end screen. Use break-all or anywhere wrapping for the email only.

findings.title: The 'your turn' cue is an 11px grey line; the big button looks the same whether MARY is talking or waiting
findings.evidence: Hold button label is 'Hold to talk to MARY' both while she speaks and when she waits (composer.tsx:94-98; log-voice-desktop.json shows hold='Hold to talk to MARY' with status 'MARY is speaking · hold to cut in' and then 'Hold the button or the space bar…'). Only the status line changes, and it is text-[0.7rem], muted (composer.tsx:303). Compare shots/voice-desktop-08-mid-welcome.png with shots/voice-desktop-10-your-turn.png. During the 1.8 s gap between her two beats the status still says 'MARY is speaking' while she is silent (shots/voice-ios-09-between-beats.png).
findings.user_impact: First-time voice users don't know when to answer. Some talk over her and cut her off; others wait in silence.
findings.recommendation: Show distinct floor states on the primary control: 'MARY is talking…' (muted, subtle waveform), then 'Your turn: hold to answer' (full colour, one pulse, optional haptic via navigator.vibrate on Android). Raise the status text to at least 14px. With Retell, drive the same states from the SDK's agent start/stop-talking and transcript events. The hold button goes away, but the listening/your-turn state still has to be designed.

findings.title: The landing page doesn't prepare visitors for the mic prompt, what MARY will ask, or how long the call really takes
findings.evidence: Landing text (log-landing-ios.json): 'Meet MARY. Your AI Revenue Concierge. Talk to her for two minutes…'. It has no mic pre-prompt, and start() goes straight to getUserMedia (mary-app.tsx:517). The preview bubble 'Hi, I'm MARY. Want first access…' (landing.tsx:9) is not what she says; the live opener was 'Hello. I'm MARY, Omnikom's AI Revenue Concierge. OmniSuite is the AI and human revenue engine…'. The 'two minutes' claim versus the docs/mary-voice.md §10 worked example (10 MARY turns, 19 beats, 243 words): at the measured 0.42 s/word, 2.98 s turn latency and 1.28 s TTS start, plus 1.8 s follow-up gaps, that is about 3.1 min even for a terse caller (worked-example.txt). What OmniSuite does appears only in the 0.7rem footer. web.dev permissions guidance: 'preface the permission prompt with why the prompt is needed' (web.dev/articles/permissions-best-practices, 2024).
findings.user_impact: The native mic sheet appears without warning, expectations (2 min, 'first access') don't match the call, and the headline sells the agent rather than the visitor's benefit, which lowers Start and allow rates.
findings.recommendation: Under the CTA add: 'Your browser will ask for the microphone. About 3 minutes. She'll ask your name, business and email.' Replace the preview bubble with her real opener. Add a one-line benefit ('Early access + launch pricing for teams that live on leads'). With Retell the mic stays open for the whole call, so the priming copy must say so, and lower latency shortens the call only slightly because about 100 s of it is her speech.

findings.title: 'Type instead' opens a voice call: MARY speaks aloud, Hold is the primary control, the copy says hold
findings.evidence: typeinstead-ios run: MARY's greeting plays with sound (voiceOff stays false: start(false) only sets listening 'paused', mary-app.tsx:532). Hold button and 'Hold the button while you talk' status are still primary, 'Can't hear her? … Play sound' shows, and the text box is 'Or type your answer' (shots/typeinstead-ios-10-your-turn.png). On phones the input is not focused (focusComposer only when hasFinePointer, mary-app.tsx:488-492).
findings.user_impact: People who chose typing because they are in a quiet or public place get a talking bot and a voice UI. They have to find the voice toggle and tap the text box before they can answer.
findings.recommendation: Make 'Type instead' a real chat mode: start with voiceOff true (keep the toggle), hide the Hold button, show the running transcript as chat bubbles, and focus the input after her first line. With Retell this path stays on /api/turn (docs/architecture/retell-migration.md:29,83), so it must be kept and polished separately.

findings.title: The iPhone call opens with a 'Can't hear her?' troubleshooting row before she has said anything
findings.evidence: shots/voice-ios-06-after-tap-1250ms.png: while the screen still shows '…' (Thinking), the row 'Can't hear her? Turn the volume up and tap Play sound. [Play sound] I can hear her' is already visible. It stays for the first 3 answers (mary-app.tsx:354-370, 'answers < 3').
findings.user_impact: The first thing an iPhone visitor sees is a hint that the product might be broken, which primes doubt and adds 3 controls to an already dense bottom area.
findings.recommendation: Show the row only after her first line has been playing for about 2 s and the visitor hasn't interacted. Collapse it to a small speaker icon after the first answer. With Retell, keep a fallback that calls the SDK's startAudioPlayback() inside a tap (docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call), but only when audio is actually blocked.

findings.title: There is no way to end the call; closing the tab silently saves the partial transcript
findings.evidence: Call header controls are only the talk-mode toggle and the voice toggle (src/features/mary/ui/call-stage.tsx:142-176); the button list for the call stage in log-voice-desktop.json has no end or leave control. On tab close or background, lead-lifecycle.ts flush beacons outcome 'abandoned' with the transcript and any captured fields (mary-app.tsx:400-413).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who wants out has to close the tab, gets no closure, and has their partial answers stored without being told.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'End' button in the call header. On tap, finalize as 'abandoned' and show a short end screen: 'Want launch news anyway? [email]' plus 'Delete what I said'. With Retell, End must call the SDK's stop and the webhook must record the outcome.

findings.title: One 'not now' ends the funnel with no lighter option to capture
findings.evidence: Prompt: 'if they want off the call, let them go warmly and set declined true' (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:156, and :119 EXIT). The declined screen offers only 'Keep talking to MARY' or 'Start over' (end-screen.tsx:107-131; shots/declined-ios-21-end-settled.png). The mocked decline posted a row with every field empty (log-declined-ios.json).
findings.user_impact: Visitors who are curious but short on time leave with nothing captured, even though an email-only signup is the cheapest conversion.
findings.recommendation: On the declined screen add one field: 'Just want launch news? Leave your email' -> /api/lead with outcome 'updates_only'. In the prompt (and the Retell port), offer this once before EXIT.

findings.title: Share previews and the canonical URL point at a domain that does not resolve (omnikom.ai)
findings.evidence: src/routes/index.tsx:8 SITE_URL = 'https://omnisuite.omnikom.ai'. The live HTML serves og:image, og:url, twitter:image and canonical on .ai (ux-audit/funnel/live.html). dns.google: omnisuite.omnikom.ai -> NXDOMAIN (Status 3), omnisuite.omnikom.io -> 185.158.133.1; https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/og-omnisuite.jpg returns 200.
findings.user_impact: Links shared on LinkedIn, WhatsApp or iMessage (the conference and referral channel) show no preview image, and search engines are told the page lives on a dead domain.
findings.recommendation: Set SITE_URL to https://omnisuite.omnikom.io (or read it from an env var) and re-check with a link-preview debugger.

findings.title: Call-screen polish: optional Phone shown as a required step, jargon pills, unlabeled mode toggle on phones
findings.evidence: Progress pills list all six WAITLIST_FIELDS including 'Phone' (optional per docs/mary-voice.md §4) and 'Operations' (src/features/mary/ui/progress-pills.tsx:17-45). On phones the 'Quiet room? Go hands-free' label is hidden and only a radio icon remains (call-stage.tsx:161, 'hidden sm:inline'). See shots/voice-ios-08-mid-welcome.png.
findings.user_impact: The pills make the call feel like a six-field form and suggest the phone number is mandatory. The unlabeled icon invites mis-taps that switch the talk mode.
findings.recommendation: Show phone as '(optional)' or hide it until asked. Rename 'Operations' to 'How you work'. Give the mode toggle a visible short label on phones ('Hands-free').

findings.title: The CTA is held back about 1-2 s by a fixed boot screen and staggered entrance animations
findings.evidence: MIN_BOOT_MS 900 + BOOT_FADE_MS 500 (mary-app.tsx:78-79) and CTA entrance delay 0.4 s + 0.7 s (landing.tsx:77-81,142-145). The page renders client-only, so the SSR HTML has no text (routes/index.tsx:37-42; live.html has no body copy). Measured: Start button in the DOM 2.6 s after navigation on a fast connection (log-landing-ios.json) and 3.0-3.2 s on throttled slow 4G with 348 KB transferred (slow-net.mjs).
findings.user_impact: On congested conference wifi the visitor stares at 'Preparing your conversation' before the value proposition appears.
findings.recommendation: Drop MIN_BOOT_MS to 0 once the app has hydrated, shorten the CTA delay, and server-render the static landing copy so the headline and CTA paint with the HTML.

visual.summary:
Lens: visual design, motion, accessibility and performance. I drove the LIVE production build (https://omnisuite.omnikom.io) and, for comparison, the repo at HEAD (local dev at 390x844). Every /api route and server function was mocked, so I made 0 live AI calls and 0 lead POSTs. I captured landing, call and end screens at 375x667, 390x844, 768x1024 and 1440x900, each in light, dark and reduced motion, plus 375x548, 700x900, landscape 844x390/667x375 and emulated safe-area insets. I ran axe-core 4.13, a keyboard-only walk, layout-shift observers, a frame-by-frame caption probe, rAF/long-task/LoAF/CDP perf sampling, and computed contrast from the OKLCH tokens. All scripts, screenshots and JSON are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/ (call it V/ below).

Verdict: the base is sound. Text contrast is 7.7-18.8:1 on the main pairs, CLS stays under 0.1 everywhere, landing and end pass axe, and the orb's JavaScript costs only 6-12 ms/s. It is not flawless yet:
- On phones the caption area overflows on most two-beat turns. The visitor's echoed words get squashed or clipped and "Show conversation" disappears.
- The old caption ghosts over the new one for about 330 ms on every turn.
- The iPhone "Can't hear her?" row makes the hold button jump 52 px.
- Reduced motion is ignored by motion/react.
- The conversation panel is not a real modal, and the end confirmation is never announced to screen readers.
- Two trust problems: the live UI is built from code that is in no git ref (44 className differences), and the share-card/canonical URLs point to a domain that does not exist.

Retell keeps this UI ("the screen, orb, progress and end screen are ours"), so most call-screen fixes have to carry over. Retell also changes the plumbing the orb, caption and pills rely on: agent-only audio level, and a separate optional transcript socket with no exact word timing.

findings.title: Caption area overflows on phones: the visitor's echoed words get sliced and 'Show conversation' is pushed out of view
findings.evidence:
V/caption-seq-390.json (live, 390x844, final settled state): the caption box is scrollHeight 182 vs clientHeight 136, the 'You · …' echo

is squashed to 0 px high, and 'Show conversation' starts at top 142 in a 136-px box, so it is fully hidden. Screenshots: V/shots/390x844-light-7-call-long-caption.png and V/shots/375x667-light-7-call-long-caption.png (half-height echo line). Repo version: V/repo/repo-390x844-light-7-call-long-caption.png (echo clipped on both sides, starts mid-word 'Realty, we're…'). Code: src/features/mary/ui/call-stage.tsx:194 fixed h-[10.5rem] + overflow-hidden (live uses h-[8.5rem]); :214 'max-w-xl truncate' inside an items-center column.
findings.user_impact: Whenever MARY answers in two beats after a longer answer, the visitor can no longer read what they said, and the only way to open the transcript disappears. A voice UI that loses the user's own words looks broken.
findings.recommendation: In call-stage.tsx, give the echo `shrink-0 max-w-full line-clamp-1` (drop max-w-xl truncate) so it keeps its line height. Clamp the current line (`line-clamp-3`) and the previous line (`line-clamp-1`, hide it below sm). Move 'Show conversation' out of the clipped box, for example into the header next to the voice toggle or as a chip beside the composer. Alternatively, make the box `flex-1 min-h-0` with a top fade mask (styles.css already has an unused trail-fade utility, :174).

findings.title: The live UI is built from code that is in no git ref (44 className differences), with fixes and regressions in both directions
findings.evidence: V/drift.mjs compares the live bundle V/live/routes-DZfdjxLS.js (downloaded 2026-09-26) with src/features/mary/ui/*: 44 live-only classNames. `git log --all -S` finds none of them in any ref, including origin/main 44318ba. Examples: live textarea 'text-sm' vs repo composer.tsx:284 'text-base … sm:text-sm'; live 'Start another conversation' has 'min-h-11' vs repo end-screen.tsx:180 'text-xs' (measured 150x16 tap target in V/repo/run-repo-390x844-light.json); live caption box h-[8.5rem] vs repo 10.5rem; live status line text-[0.62rem] vs repo 0.7rem (composer.tsx:303). The live bundle has no wakeLock code, which is consistent with PR #1 plus unsynced Lovable-side UI edits.
findings.user_impact: Any UI fix made in GitHub, including PR #2 and the Retell UI work, starts from a baseline visitors do not see. The next Lovable publish from GitHub will silently revert the live mobile compaction (e.g. 44-px header targets), or Lovable's edits will overwrite repo fixes.
findings.recommendation: Before merging PR #2, pull Lovable's current project state into GitHub (Lovable's GitHub sync, or copy the live component code into a branch). Diff it, choose per class, and only then apply the findings below. Add a CI check or checklist step that compares the deployed bundle hash with the build of main.

findings.title: Live typing box is 14 px on phones, so iPhone Safari zooms the whole call screen when it is tapped
findings.evidence: V/textarea.mjs on live, 390x844 iPhone UA: computed textarea font-size 14px, class 'max-h-24 … text-sm'. The viewport meta has no maximum-scale (src/routes/__root.tsx:84). The repo has the correct 16 px (composer.tsx:284 'text-base … sm:text-sm'), so this is a live-only regression. Sources: https://defensivecss.dev/tip/input-zoom-safari/ and https://css-tricks.com/16px-or-larger-text-prevents-ios-form-zoom/ (Safari zooms focused inputs rendered below 16 px and does not zoom back out).
findings.user_impact: People who choose 'Type instead' (loud rooms, mic denied) see the page zoom in on focus. The header, orb and hold button slide off-screen and the page stays zoomed after sending, which feels broken on the fallback path.
findings.recommendation: Restore text-base (16 px) on the textarea below sm, as in the repo, when the live code is reconciled. Check any other input the owner vault uses.

findings.title: Share card and canonical URL point to omnisuite.omnikom.ai, which does not exist (NXDOMAIN)
findings.evidence: Live HTML (V/live/index.html) has og:image https://omnisuite.omnikom.ai/og-omnisuite.jpg, og:url and rel=canonical on the same host. https://dns.google/resolve?name=omnisuite.omnikom.ai returns Status 3 (NXDOMAIN), and so does omnikom.ai. The image exists at https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/og-omnisuite.jpg (200, 58,131 bytes). Code: src/routes/index.tsx:8 SITE_URL.
findings.user_impact: Every link shared in iMessage, WhatsApp, LinkedIn or Slack shows no preview image. Search engines are told the canonical page lives on a dead domain. This is the first impression for most referred visitors.
findings.recommendation: Set SITE_URL in src/routes/index.tsx:8 to https://omnisuite.omnikom.io, or derive it from the request host. Re-check with a link-preview debugger after deploy.

findings.title: The previous caption ghosts over the new one for about 330 ms on every turn, even with reduced motion
findings.evidence: V/caption-seq-390.json rows t=725-1062 and t=3245-3562: the exiting line is position:absolute (AnimatePresence mode="popLayout") at opacity 0.95→0 while the new line fades in at the same spot. Screenshots: V/shots/390x844-light-8-call-after3.png, V/shots/1440x900-light-8-call-after3.png, V/shots/390x844-light-reduced-8-call-after3.png, V/repo/repo-390x844-light-8-call-after3.png (both texts overlap). Code: call-stage.tsx:195 and :222 popLayout; exit {opacity:0, y:-10} is applied even when reduced.
findings.user_impact: Every reply starts with two sentences printed on top of each other, the most visible 'unpolished' moment on the main screen.
findings.recommendation: For the caption use mode="wait" with a 120-150 ms opacity-only exit, or crossfade in a grid cell (both children in `grid-area:1/1`) so they never overlap spatially. Drop the y offset when reduced.

findings.title: iPhone 'Can't hear her?' row is on from the first second, and removing it makes the hold button jump 52 px
findings.evidence: The row is shown before MARY has said anything (V/shots/390x844-light-2-call-thinking.png) and stays for the first 3 answers (src/features/mary/mary-app.tsx:350-368). When it goes away, a layout-shift entry records: orb canvas 117→143, composer height 201→149, hold button top 454→506 (V/run-375x667-light.json, t=24024, value 0.051). The same happens at 390x844 (V/run-390x844-light.json, 631→683). This contradicts composer.tsx:205-206 ('the button never moves under a thumb'), because the hint renders below the textarea (composer.tsx:320).
findings.user_impact: On every iPhone call a warning sits under the controls while MARY is clearly audible (the operator confirmed audio works). Just after the third answer, the button a thumb is resting on moves 52 px down, which invites mis-taps and makes the screen feel jumpy.
findings.recommendation: Reserve a fixed-height slot for all notices: min-h on the notice container, or absolutely position the hint above the hold button with a fade. Show the row only after her first line has finished playing with no reaction, or collapse it to one 'Can't hear? Tap to play' chip.

findings.title: Words MARY has not spoken yet sit at 1.57:1 contrast (axe: serious)
findings.evidence: axe color-contrast violations on the call screen in V/run-390x844-light.json (call.axe): fg #cbcac7 on #fbfaf7 = 1.57:1 at 20 px (4.5:1 required) and at 26.4 px on desktop (3:1 required). V/contrast.mjs: ink over the page reaches 3.12:1 at alpha 0.45 and 5.13:1 at 0.6. Code: call-stage.tsx:22 'opacity-20'. The full line is painted ghosted from the moment it is added, before any audio (V/shots/390x844-light-3-call-speaking-start.png).
findings.user_impact: Low-vision readers, and anyone in sunlight, cannot read ahead or read along. During the speech start delay the whole sentence shows as a faint grey block.
findings.recommendation: Either raise unrevealed words to opacity ≥0.6 on phones (≥0.45 at ≥24 px) and keep the karaoke contrast step small, or do not paint unrevealed words and reserve their space with `invisible`, so words appear as she says them.

findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion is not honoured by motion/react: the orb still flies and scales between screens
findings.evidence: V/motion-probe.mjs with reducedMotion=reduce: 58 distinct orb positions over about 650 ms after Start (216→203 px, y 253→184), the same spring as without reduce. There is no MotionConfig anywhere in src (grep). Motion's docs say the default reducedMotion is "never", and "user" disables transform and layout animations while keeping opacity (https://motion.dev/docs/react-motion-config). Only some components guard `initial` with useReducedMotion. layoutId sits at call-stage.tsx:188 and landing/end screens, and exit y offsets are not guarded.
findings.user_impact: Visitors who asked their OS for less motion still get the shared-element flight and sliding caption exits on every screen change and every turn.
findings.recommendation: Wrap <LayoutGroup> in mary-app.tsx with <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">. This removes the layout, transform and y animations globally, keeps the opacity fades, and makes most per-component `reduced ? … :` branches unnecessary.

findings.title: The orb redraws at 60 fps in every state, forever, including the static end screen
findings.evidence:
V/perf-ios-x1-no-preference.json vs V/perf-ios-x1-reduce.json (same flow, orb static when reduced):
- End screen idle: 482 vs 242 rAF callbacks in 4 s, so the orb adds 60 frames/s indefinitely.
- Main-thread busy (CDP TaskDuration): landing 97% vs 1.3%, speaking 93.6% vs 3.2%, end 52.6% vs 2.7%.
- With CPU throttled 4x (V/perf-ios-x4-no-preference.json): about 40 fps, p50 33 ms on the landing.
- Orb JavaScript is small (5.9-11.6 ms/s), so the cost is GPU presentation.
- The runner uses SwiftShader software GL, so absolute numbers apply to software-GL devices, not iPhone 13.
- Also: a 1348-ms long task during load at 4x, 131-184 ms frames right after Start, while the orb flight animates.
Code: mary-orb.tsx:134-157 (loop never idles); orb-renderer.ts:70 antialias:true although the shader already anti-aliases the edge with smoothstep; mary-orb.tsx:101 DPR cap 1.5 (324x324 canvas at 390 px).
findings.user_impact: Constant GPU work drains phone battery on a page people leave open after signing up. On software-GL or low-end devices it causes dropped frames exactly during transitions and speech.
findings.recommendation:
In mary-orb.tsx:
- Stop the loop in 'done' about 2 s after the bloom settles.
- Drop to ~24-30 fps in idle/listening, and use full rate only while speaking or hearing.
- Pause the landing orb after ~10 s without interaction.
In orb-renderer.ts:70, set antialias:false and powerPreference:'low-power'.
Fall back to the 2D or static frame when the renderer string contains 'SwiftShader' or when frame p95 exceeds 25 ms.

findings.title: 'Conversation so far' panel is not a real modal, and focus is pulled into the composer behind it

- Add an sr-only <h1> 'Talking with MARY' on the call screen.

findings.title: The screen reader reads MARY's whole line the instant her voice starts, so two voices talk over each other
findings.evidence: call-stage.tsx:181-184 announces `MARY: ${current.text}` through aria-live=polite. voice-line.ts:96-97 adds the line to the store before speak() starts, so VoiceOver or NVDA speech overlaps MARY's TTS. The orb's role=img label says 'MARY is speaking' on the silent landing (landing.tsx:103).

findings.recommendation: When voice is on, announce only the visitor-relevant state ('MARY is speaking', 'Your turn') and not the text. Offer a 'Read captions aloud' option, or announce the text when voiceOff is true. Keep one always-mounted status region for notices instead of mounting role=status nodes. Label the landing orb as decorative (aria-hidden).

findings.title: Retell changes the data the orb, caption and pills are built on; design for it now

Retell web-call docs (fetched 2026-09-26, V/../../retell/deploy_web-call.md):
- :158 — onAudio snapshots 'contain incoming audio', i.e. the agent only, with no visitor level for the 'hearing you' state.

- :129 — the transcript socket is optional and 'This failure does not fire onError'.
SDK 3.0.1 base-session.ts:290-297 allocates a new Float32Array(fftSize) and emits it on every animation frame. Option B gives the browser no structured fields mid-call (docs/architecture/retell-migration.md step 5: fields arrive only via save_lead). URL: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call

If the current UI is rewired as-is:

- The pills stay empty until the end.

reliability.summary: I forced each failure against the local dev server with every /api/* and /_serverFn route mocked, using the iPhone 13 profile plus a desktop profile for the double-click test. I also read mary-app.tsx, conversation/*, voice/*, lead-sync, lead-lifecycle, the API routes and Code.gs. I made 0 live AI calls. The only live requests were GET /api/lead and static bundle files. Scripts, JSON logs and 74 screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/. The healthy path works: sign-up by holding or typing, cutting in while she speaks, switching tabs or locking the phone and coming back, and reopening the mic after its track dies. When something fails, though, the app almost never tells the visitor the truth, and it has no path that works without AI. A replay of the 2026-09-23 outage gives an opening line that apologises for "losing my train of thought", then "Didn't catch that" for every hold, then typed answers that get no reply at all. Hung requests, a 150 ms brush of the Hold button, or an empty transcript each leave MARY silent or stuck on "Thinking…" indefinitely. The biggest problem is outside the voice code: the live site reports {"configured":false} for the lead sheet, yet the end screen shows "Early access confirmed, position #707", a number made from a hash of the email. Every lead today stays only in the visitor's own browser. Retell removes the speech-to-text, text-to-speech and turn-taking failures. The lead delivery, honest end-screen copy, mic-error wording, the no-AI fallback, the Start guard and failure telemetry are ours and must be carried into Retell. GAP-REGISTER.md, which the task asked me to read, is not in the repo on any branch.

findings.title: Live site sends no lead anywhere, but tells the visitor they are confirmed with a made-up position
findings.evidence: curl https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/api/lead -> {"configured":false} (2026-09-26). lead-lifecycle.ts:124-125 turns that into sync "local". The position comes from waitlist-store.ts:122-125 (128 + hash % 640). Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s01-end-unconfigured.png shows 'EARLY ACCESS CONFIRMED · You're on the list, Sam · Early access position #707'. PROJECT-STATE.md:64: Apps Script deployed, SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL never set.
findings.user_impact: Every visitor who signs up on the live site today is lost to the operator; the lead exists only in the visitor's own localStorage. The visitor is still promised a queue position that nothing backs.
findings.recommendation: Now: set SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL + SHEETS_WEBAPP_SECRET in Lovable and run one real call end to end. In code: show a position only when sync==='sheet'. For sync 'local' or 'failed', use honest copy ("We've got your details") and give /api/lead a server-side fallback store (e.g. Cloudflare KV/D1, or an email to the operator) so a lead never lives only in the visitor's browser (lead-lifecycle.ts:124-132, end-screen.tsx:74-102).

findings.title: During an AI outage MARY loops on apologies with no fallback, and the lead is never captured
findings.evidence: Replay of 2026-09-23 (.claude/POSITION.md:81: turn 200 {"type":"error"}, speech and transcribe 502, fallback server function 500). Screenshots s02-error-line-1-welcome.png through -7 and s02-502-*.png in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/. The opening line is 'Sorry — I lost my train of thought there. Could you say that once more?' (mary-stream.ts:126-128), cut off at 'Could you say' in the caption box. Holds get 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' because transcribe 502 is turned into '' at audio-engine.ts:2171. In the 502 variant every message gets 'I hit a snag on my side' (turn-runner.ts:34,185-186). When the tab closes, the beacon carries name '' and email '' (s02-error-line.json).
findings.user_impact: For the hours of an outage, every visitor gets a broken, apologising MARY with no voice and a hint to check their own volume. They can never finish; the name and email they type are never pulled out of the text, and with no sheet configured nothing reaches the operator.
findings.recommendation: Count consecutive turn failures in TurnRunner. After 2, replace the conversation with a no-AI inline form ("MARY's line is down — leave your name and email and the team will follow up") that POSTs to /api/lead. Add a cheap GET /api/health that checks the gateway, so the landing can offer 'type or leave details' before Start. Treat non-2xx/timeouts from transcribe as a service error, not 'speak closer'.

findings.title: Near-repeat filter can swallow her whole reply: typed answers get no reply and the orb stays on 'thinking'
findings.evidence: s02-error-line-4-typed1.png, -5-typed2.png, -6-typed2-plus15s.png, -7-typed3.png: after each typed answer there is no MARY line, the caption shows '…' and the status says 'Thinking…' 15+ s later. Network log: /api/turn, then the /_serverFn retry fails, then nothing is spoken. turn-runner.ts:129-152 skips a reply that is a near-repeat of an earlier line even after the retry fails. Presence is set to thinking at turn-runner.ts:100 and nothing resets it when no line is said.
findings.user_impact: The visitor types, sees '…' forever and does not know whether to wait, retype or leave. The same thing can happen with a healthy gateway whenever the model repeats itself twice.
findings.recommendation: Never end a turn without output: if the final line is suppressed, say a rotating short bridge or show an inline 'MARY didn't answer — Retry' chip, and reset presence to idle in the finally block. Vary the fallback copy so the retry isn't itself a near-repeat.

findings.title: One hung request freezes the call for good, and messages typed meanwhile vanish
findings.evidence: /api/turn and the fallback both hang: 'MARY … / Thinking…' at 5, 14, 18, 30, 60 and 90 s (s03-turn-fn-hang-*.png). A message typed at 30 s never appeared on screen and no request was ever sent (s03-turn-fn-hang.json). Causes: the fallback maryTurn has no timeout (mary-stream.ts:46-54, and mary.functions.ts:595 streamText has no abortSignal), and ADD_LINE runs inside the serial queue (turn-runner.ts:65-71, 83-91). A transcription hang gives 45 s of 'Thinking…' (s04-transcribe-hang-45s.png): no signal on the client fetch (audio-engine.ts:2170) and no upstream timeout (routes/api/transcribe.ts:33-37).
findings.user_impact: A slow or stuck upstream silently kills the conversation. The visitor's own words disappear from the screen, which reads as the app ignoring them.
findings.recommendation: Put AbortSignal.timeout on every client fetch (fallback turn about 12 s, transcribe about 10 s) and on the server function's streamText and the transcribe upstream fetch. Dispatch ADD_LINE for the user's message synchronously in send(), before enqueue. A newer send() should abort the in-flight turn instead of queuing behind it. On timeout, show a retry chip.

findings.title: A brush or mis-tap of the Hold button kills her turn: dead air, and what the visitor said is lost
findings.evidence: A 150 ms tap while she was thinking about 'My name is Sam Rivera': no reply ever, the name is not saved (localStorage empty) and no lead checkpoint is sent (s04-tap-while-thinking-2-after.png, -3-plus20s.png). A 150 ms brush during the greeting: she stops at 'Hi,…' and never asks her question (s04-brush-while-speaking-1.png). onPress calls runner.interrupt() before the hold is known to be real (mary-app.tsx:184-191, turn-runner.ts:78-81, 99). A hold under 300 ms only calls onCancel (hold-talk.ts:494-497). SET_COLLECTED comes after the stale check (turn-runner.ts:127,146-148). The button is a 64 px full-width bar in the thumb zone (composer.tsx:83).
findings.user_impact: A thumb resting near the bottom of the phone stalls the call with no prompt on screen. Details the visitor already gave (e.g. their name) are discarded, so MARY has to ask again.
findings.recommendation: On press, pause her line rather than stopping it. Commit the interrupt only once the hold passes MIN_HOLD_MS and produces words. On onCancel/onMissed, resume the paused line or re-run the dropped turn. Always apply turn.collected even when the turn is stale.

findings.title: Failed transcription blames the visitor, and any empty transcript leaves 'Thinking…' stuck
findings.evidence: /api/transcribe 502 comes back as '' (audio-engine.ts:2171), which shows 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' (s02-error-line-2-hold1.png). On healthy services, a hold that transcribes to 'Thank you.' or 'Bye.' is dropped by the hallucination filter (audio-engine.ts:2158-2160,2174), and the orb still says 'MARY is thinking' with the button reading 'Thinking… hold to talk' 20 s later (s04-empty-transcript-2-plus20s.png). Cause: onRelease sets thinking (mary-app.tsx:192-195), but waiting() only resets from 'hearing' (mary-app.tsx:175-179).
findings.user_impact: Visitors are told to speak closer when the service is down. After a miss, the screen claims MARY is thinking when nothing is happening, so people wait instead of pressing again. Saying 'thank you' or 'bye' is ignored.
findings.recommendation: Return an error from transcribe() for non-2xx and timeouts, and show 'I couldn't process that just now — hold again or type'. In waiting(), reset presence to idle from both 'thinking' and 'hearing'. Don't apply the hallucination filter to held clips with real peak and more than 600 ms of audio.

findings.title: End screen confirms the sign-up even when the sheet write failed, and nothing retries
findings.evidence: With /api/lead returning 500, the end screen shows 'EARLY ACCESS CONFIRMED · You're on the list, Sam. · Your details are saved. Your position comes with the confirmation.' (s01-end-500.png). finalize() sends one syncLead with a 9 s timeout and never retries (lead-lifecycle.ts:118-133, lead-sync.ts:77). Checkpoints are fire-and-forget (lead-lifecycle.ts:89-93). 'saved' copy: end-screen.tsx:93-101.
findings.user_impact: If the Apps Script blips at the final save (quota, cold start, the 9 s timeout), a completed sign-up is lost, while the visitor is told their details are saved.
findings.recommendation: Keep an outbox in localStorage keyed by sessionId. Retry with backoff (3 tries), send a beacon on pagehide, and flush the outbox on the next page load. Use honest copy while pending or failed, plus a Retry button and a contact fallback.

findings.title: Mic denied or missing gives a generic message that points to a mic button that does not exist
findings.evidence: s04-mic-denied-1-after-welcome.png and s04-no-mic-1-after-welcome.png both show 'I couldn't open the microphone. Tap the mic button to try again'. The specific message from primeMicPermission is overwritten because hold-recorder.ts:118 throws a raw DOMException, which micMessage maps to 'unknown' (text.ts:116). Hold mode renders no mic button (composer.tsx:230; measured micButton=false). Each Hold press calls getUserMedia again with no visible change (gum count 3). The in-app-browser 'Open in browser' guidance (text.ts:100-104) can never show in hold mode.
findings.user_impact: People who denied the mic, or who arrive from Instagram or LinkedIn in-app browsers, get wrong instructions and keep pressing a Hold button that cannot work. Typing still works, but nothing steers them to it clearly.
findings.recommendation: In HoldRecorder.openLine, wrap getUserMedia errors in MicUnavailableError(micFailureFrom(e)). Don't overwrite a specific mic error with 'unknown'. In hold mode, say 'hold the button to ask again'. On denied or no-device, switch to typing-first: disable Hold and show a short iOS Settings hint.

findings.title: Going offline mid-call is reported as a server snag and a broken microphone, and the error stays after recovery
findings.evidence: Offline, typed: 'I hit a snag on my side — could you try that once more?' Offline, held: the transcribe fetch throws, hold-talk.ts:505-509 calls onError, and mary-app.tsx:206-209 shows 'I couldn't open the microphone…' and sets mic.live=false, which also starts idle nudges. Back online with a normal answer, the mic error is still on screen (s04-offline-2-held-offline.png, s04-offline-3-back-online.png). No navigator.onLine or online/offline handling anywhere in src/features/mary.
findings.user_impact: On conference Wi-Fi the visitor is misled about what broke (their mic or MARY) and may give up, even though retrying would have worked.
findings.recommendation: Listen for offline/online events and show 'You're offline — I'll carry on when you're back'. Queue the typed message and send it automatically on 'online'. Route network errors away from micMessage, and clear mic.error after the next successful hold.

findings.title: Reload mid-call wipes the conversation, and the sheet's transcript gets overwritten
findings.evidence: After 2 answers and a reload: back to the landing with no 'continue', and a fresh welcome with messages=[] (only the collected fields are restored, mary-app.tsx:467-474). She reintroduces herself while the progress pills already show name and email (s04-reload-3-restarted.png). The next checkpoint sends turns:0 and a short transcript (s04-reload.json), which Code.gs:210 writes over the full transcript.
findings.user_impact: An accidental pull-to-refresh or iOS tab reload restarts the pitch, and the operator loses the pre-reload transcript.
findings.recommendation: Persist lines and flags in sessionStorage per sessionId and offer 'Pick up where you left off'. Make the Apps Script keep the longer transcript, or append to it, instead of overwriting.

findings.title: Double-clicking Start opens two mics and runs two welcomes (3 AI calls instead of 1)
findings.evidence: Desktop double-click (s04-double-tap-desk.json): 2 getUserMedia calls and 2 live mic streams, /api/turn welcome ×2 plus a /_serverFn repeat-retry, and a second greeting about 4.4 s after the first. start() checks the stage at mary-app.tsx:510 but only sets it at :531, after two awaits. primeMicPermission overwrites primedStream (audio-engine.ts:1305-1307), leaving the first stream with no owner to stop it. Not reproduced on the iPhone profile.
findings.user_impact: She greets twice, the laptop's mic indicator can stay on, and each impatient double-click adds paid calls.
findings.recommendation: Set a starting ref synchronously at the top of start() and disable both landing buttons. In primeMicPermission, share the in-flight promise instead of calling getUserMedia again.

findings.title: When the speech service hangs, every line sits dim for about 9 s; during outages the screen gives conflicting 'can't hear her' advice
findings.evidence: With /api/speech hung, the line stays at 20% opacity as 'MARY is speaking' until the 9 s first-byte guard fires (audio-engine.ts:1076-1078), and again for the follow-up (s03-speech-hang-3s/6s/9.5s/12s.png): about 19 s per two-beat turn, with a fresh request each line. During a 502, 'Can't hear her? Turn the volume up and tap Play sound' shows next to 'My voice didn't come through just now' (s02-error-line-1-welcome.png). Play sound re-requests /api/speech (audio-engine.ts:660-669).
findings.user_impact: Slow speech turns every turn into a long wait. In an outage the visitor is sent to fiddle with their volume, and each tap on Play sound is another failing paid request.
findings.recommendation: Add a circuit breaker: after one speech failure, reveal text at once and switch to voice-off for 60 s with a 'Voice unavailable — reading mode' note. Lower the first-byte guard to about 4 s. Hide silentHint while voiceFailed is shown.

findings.title: Long silence never ends the call; the mic stays live and PR #2's wake lock keeps the screen on
findings.evidence: 90 s after the welcome in hold mode: no nudge, no timeout, 1 live mic stream (s04-silence-0.png vs s04-silence-90s.png). Idle nudges only run when the mic is not live or is muted (mary-app.tsx:378-398). The wake lock is held for the whole call (mary-app.tsx:274-286).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who walks away leaves a phone awake with the mic indicator on. No partial lead is written if they gave no field.
findings.recommendation: After about 45 s with no press, speak one gentle nudge. After about 3 min, show 'Still there? Continue / Leave your email', release the mic and wake lock, and flush the lead as abandoned.

findings.title: No client telemetry on handled failures: outages are only found by hand
findings.evidence: Only the root error boundary reports (__root.tsx:37-42, lovable-error-reporting.ts). The window.__lovableEvents.track type exists but is never called. error-capture.ts is server-only. Turn fallbacks, SNAG lines, speech onError, transcribe non-2xx and lead sync 'failed' are never reported. The 2026-09-23 outage was found by manual probing (.claude/POSITION.md:81).
findings.user_impact: The operator cannot see that visitors are hitting broken calls, so an outage can run for hours (as on 2026-09-23).
findings.recommendation: Send small events (turn_fallback, speech_failed, transcribe_failed, lead_sync_failed, mic_error with the reason) via __lovableEvents.track or a /api/event beacon. Add an hourly synthetic check of /api/turn and /api/speech with alerting.

findings.title: Live build has no screen wake lock (PR #2 adds it), and Retell's SDK will not add one either
findings.evidence: The live bundle https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/assets/routes-DZfdjxLS.js contains no 'wakeLock' (grep, 2026-09-26). PR #2 adds it at mary-app.tsx:51-75. retell-client-js-sdk 3.0.1 (npm, published 2026-09-08) src has no wakeLock or visibilitychange handling (scratchpad/retell/client/package/src).
findings.user_impact: On the live site, an iPhone that auto-locks mid-call suspends her voice and the mic.
findings.recommendation: Merge and publish PR #2. Keep holdScreenAwake around the Retell call (request it in the Start tap, re-acquire it on visibilitychange).

findings.title: Retry notices stay up after the visitor switches to typing
findings.evidence: 'Didn't catch that…' and 'Loud in here? Type your answer below instead.' remain after typed messages and cover the caption area (s02-error-line-6-typed2-plus15s.png). send() (mary-app.tsx:538-544) does not clear missedHold or suggestTyping, unlike onText (mary-app.tsx:196-199).
